00_phase0/requirements_matrix.md

Requirements Matrix — PadCare Complaint Management Assessment

Source of truth: PadCare – Product Analyst (Process & Systems) Take-Home Assessment (PDF, not committed to this repo). Status values: Not started · In progress · Done · Verified (passed Phase 8 audit).

G. Submission-level requirements

Req ID Assessment requirement Required output Planned implementation Validation method Status
G-01 "One Word/PDF document covering all three tasks, with embedded or linked diagrams" Single .docx + .pdf Phase 9 assembles all phase outputs; diagram embedded as image Open PDF; check all 3 tasks + diagram present Not started
G-02 "At the top… an Assumptions section listing every meaningful assumption" Assumptions section, first pages Curated from assumptions_register.md (only meaningful ones, grouped) Every assumption referenced in Tasks 1–3 appears in the section Not started
G-03 "At the top… a Challenges Map… mapping each of the 8 Current Challenges to the part of your design that addresses it" Table, 8 rows, near top challenges_map.md (Phase 3), condensed for doc 8/8 rows; each cites a specific stage/field, not a generic phrase Verified
G-04 "What we expect at the end of every task: a short 'Reasoning' note (3–6 lines)" 3 reasoning notes One per task, written last, explaining why + trade-off Line count 3–6; contains a trade-off or limitation Done — candidate rewrite
G-05 Design anchored in the 8 challenges and 5 complaints; "Generic answers will read as generic" Whole document Every major decision cites a challenge (C-x) or scenario (S-x) Phase 8 audit: no decision without a C/S anchor Verified
G-06 "Quality over volume… Diagrams beat paragraphs. Reasoning beats output." Concise doc Tables and diagram over prose; working files stay out of final doc Page count target 8–12 (working target, not a brief requirement) Not started
G-07 "State your assumptions. Whenever the brief is silent… write it down and proceed." Labelled assumptions inline + register Tag [A-xx] inline wherever an assumption is used Every [A-xx] tag resolves in register Verified
G-08 Avoid "ITSM frameworks, P1/P2/P3 tiers, standard CRM screens" Design vocabulary PadCare-specific severity names and rules (see D-04) Search final doc for P1/P2/P3 / ITIL jargon Verified
G-09 Avoid "Designing only the happy path" Exception paths Exception states in lifecycle; exceptions section in Task 3 Each lifecycle state has ≥1 exit for failure; Task 3 covers 3 named exceptions Verified
G-10 Internal consistency: "Task 2's walk-throughs and Task 3's spec actually work inside the design from Task 1. Nothing dangles." Consistent doc Phase 8 cross-phase audit consistency_audit.md with zero open issues Verified
G-11 If incomplete: "What I finished and what I didn't" note at top Conditional note Add only if any task is incomplete at submission Check before export Not started
G-12 Candidate must defend choices in a 30–45 min walkthrough Interview prep Phase 10 prep pack; candidate makes the judgement calls Candidate can explain each decision in decision_log.md unaided Not started

C. The eight current challenges (each must be explicitly addressed)

Req ID Assessment requirement Required output Planned implementation Validation method Status
C-01 Complaints lost between channels (WhatsApp to one CS person invisible to team; lost on leave) Mechanism for central capture and shared visibility Single register; mandatory logging by whoever receives it; team queue, not personal inbox S1–S5 each enter via a named channel and land in the register Verified
C-02 Repeat vs new unknown (3rd "bad odour" from same site in two months) Repeat detection Related-record search at intake (customer + site + category + window); repeat count shown Test case: repeat suggestion fires Verified
C-03 Service requests, status checks, account concerns all called "complaints" Classification model Separate record types with separate flows/closure rules S1–S5 map to distinct types without ambiguity Verified
C-04 No clear handoff (billing: CS → Finance → CS; sits in nobody's inbox) Ownership and handoff rules One accountable owner; tracked handoff with acknowledgement + escalation S2 walkthrough shows every handoff with owner and timer Verified
C-05 "Resolved" ≠ resolved; no customer-confirmed closure Closure model Resolution evidence + Awaiting Customer Confirmation state; reopen path Test case: cannot close without evidence/confirmation Verified
C-06 Can't see patterns (e.g., 40% missed services in one city) Structured data Structured category/sub-category, city, site, timestamps; metric definitions The "40% in one city" question is answerable from fields Verified
C-07 Customer has no visibility; "any update?" follow-ups Customer update mechanism Proactive updates at defined status changes, by CS (v1); portal deferred S4 is handled by linking, and the design reduces S4-type volume Verified
C-08 Severity by who shouts loudest, not impact Severity model Impact-based rules; reporter seniority not an input Same issue from CXO vs facility manager → same severity Verified

S. The five sample complaints (all must be handled)

Req ID Complaint (verbatim) Assessment's own label Planned implementation Validation method Status
S-01 "Collection was not collected this month. Please plan the visit ASAP, as it's a hygiene issue." Operational Operational complaint; hygiene-impact severity rule Classification table + optional Task 2 walkthrough Verified
S-02 "Your invoice for September shows charges for the Hyderabad site, but we shifted to a new location in July. Please correct the address." Billing Billing complaint; CS → Finance → CS handoff; possibly also site master data correction Mandatory Task 2 candidate; test cases Verified
S-03 "We need an additional disposal unit installed on our 4th floor — the existing one is overflowing daily." "A service request in disguise" Split: service request (new unit) + linked operational complaint (overflow) — to be stress-tested in Phase 1 Classification table shows split rule Verified
S-04 "Just checking — has my complaint from last week about the missed service been resolved? No one has updated me." Status check Status enquiry linked to existing record; does not create new complaint; flags missed-update failure Exception case in Task 3 Verified
S-05 "Service quality has dropped across multiple sites in our portfolio. We need a meeting to discuss." Account-level concern Account-level record owned by KAM; multi-site; closure = agreed action plan Classification table + optional Task 2 walkthrough Verified

E. Evaluation criteria (used as audit lenses in Phase 8)

Req ID Criterion What they look for How we'll check
E-01 Engagement with the actual problem Responds to 8 challenges + 5 complaints C-01…C-08 and S-01…S-05 all Verified
E-02 Reasoning quality Explains why; trade-offs; limitations Each reasoning note has a "because" and a trade-off
E-03 Process clarity Logical stages, decision points; followable by outsider Cold read of diagram by someone unfamiliar
E-04 Requirement completeness Fields, validations, conditions, exceptions; developer needs no basic follow-ups Developer-question checklist in Phase 8
E-05 Internal consistency Task 2/3 work inside Task 1 consistency_audit.md
E-06 Communication Organised, skimmable, no fluff, assumptions upfront Page count; table density; no paragraph > 5 lines

Positive signals called out explicitly in the brief

  • Variety in the 5 complaints treated as the central design problem (→ record-type model, Phase 1).
  • Challenges Map at the top that connects each problem to a specific design choice (→ G-03).
  • Task 2 walkthrough that catches and flags an inconsistency in our own design (→ T2-D2, design_review.md).
  • Task 3 validations that clearly come from the complaint examples, not a template (→ trace each validation to S-x).
  • Explicit trade-offs: "I could do X or Y; here's why X" (→ decision log format).

Negative signals called out explicitly

  • Generic ITSM / P1-P2-P3 / standard CRM screens (→ G-08).
  • Long padded prose (→ G-06).
  • Happy path only (→ G-09).
  • Reasoning that describes instead of explains (→ G-04).

00_phase0/assumptions_register.md

Assumptions Register

Rule: anything the brief does not state is an assumption (A) or a proposed design decision (see decision_log.md). Facts come only from the brief.

Confirmed facts (from the brief, for reference)

ID Fact Brief section
F-01 24+ cities, 2,000+ customer sites, ~40,000 services/month The context
F-02 Site types: corporate offices, manufacturing units, hospitals, schools, residential complexes The context
F-03 Complaint Management module is to be built inside PadCareOne, the internal platform The context
F-04 Six intake channels: SPOC WhatsApp to CS contact; generic support email inbox; phone call to CS; CS check-in call; KAM-forwarded escalation; verbal to SE on site How complaints come in today
F-05 Seven roles and their stated responsibilities (Client SPOC, End User, CS, SE, Ops City Manager, KAM, Finance) Who is involved
F-06 CS = owns client relationship, first responder. Ops City Manager = escalation when CS cannot resolve. KAM = involved when critical or repeat. Finance = billing, credit notes, invoice corrections Who is involved
F-07 Today: no single place to log, track, prioritise, analyse The context
F-08 Today CS marks resolved when they reply; no customer-confirmed closure Challenge 5

Assumptions

Columns: Gap (what the brief doesn't say) · Assumption · Why needed · Validate with PadCare · Impact if wrong (H/M/L).

ID Gap Assumption Why needed Validate with Impact if wrong
A-01 Does PadCareOne hold customer and site master data? Yes — customer accounts and sites exist as records in PadCareOne (it runs operations for 2,000+ sites). Needed for customer–site lookup and validation at intake. Product Lead H — without it, validation becomes free text and repeat detection weakens
A-02 Does PadCareOne hold service schedules / visit records? Yes, at least a scheduled-service list per site with visit date and status. Lets the form link a "missed collection" to a specific scheduled visit (S-01, S-04). Product Lead / Ops H — affects S-01 evidence and auto-verification
A-03 Are invoices visible in PadCareOne? No assumption of integration. Invoice number is entered manually by CS; Finance verifies. S-02 needs an invoice reference. Safer not to assume a billing integration. Finance M
A-04 Do channels (WhatsApp, email, phone) integrate with PadCareOne? No. v1 = manual logging by the PadCare employee who receives the issue. Brief says complaints are "handled informally" today; no integration is mentioned. Product Lead M — integration would reduce logging effort, not change the flow
A-05 Can SEs use PadCareOne in the field? SEs have a mobile view of PadCareOne (or a lightweight form) to log verbal complaints. Channel 6 (verbal to SE) is otherwise the most likely to be lost (C-01). Ops M — fallback: SE reports to CS who logs it
A-06 Is there a customer-facing portal? No. Customers receive updates from CS via their existing channel (WhatsApp/email). Portal = future. Brief calls PadCareOne "our internal platform". Product Lead M — changes C-07 solution, not the core flow
A-07 Contractual SLAs with customers? None known. All SLA targets are proposals. Brief asks us to "propose reasonable timelines". CS Lead / KAMs M
A-08 Service frequency per site Varies; at least monthly for some sites (S-01: "this month"). Defines how fast a missed collection becomes a hygiene risk. Ops M — affects severity rule
A-09 Which CS person owns which customer? Each customer account has a named primary CS owner, plus a city/team CS queue. Needed for auto-assignment and for cover when the person is on leave (C-01). CS Lead H
A-10 Is a KAM assigned to every customer? No — only large enterprise accounts have a KAM (per role description). Routing for S-05 differs if the account has no KAM. Sales / KAM lead M
A-11 Who can approve credit notes? Finance approves; CS cannot issue credit notes. S-02 resolution path. Finance M
A-12 Working hours / calendar for SLA clocks SLAs measured in business hours (e.g., 9:00–18:00, Mon–Sat) except hygiene-critical issues, which run on calendar hours. SLA arithmetic in Task 2. Ops / CS L
A-13 Volume of complaints Unknown. Not used to size anything; design must not depend on it. Avoids inventing figures. CS L
A-14 Is a site relocation (S-02) already reflected in master data? Unknown — S-02 implies it may not be. Design treats "site moved but master not updated" as a real exception. S-02 likely has a root cause in master data, not only in the invoice. Finance / Ops M
A-15 Is there a CS Lead / CS manager role? Not relied on — the brief does not list one. Escalations use only the roles in the brief. Keeps routing within known roles. CS M — would be a natural owner for cover and unowned queues
A-16 Does an additional unit change charges/contract? Possibly; the service request flow includes an optional commercial approval by the KAM (or CS where there is no KAM). S-03 fulfilment path. Sales / Finance M
A-17 Complaints from before go-live Not migrated. When a customer chases one, it is created then, flagged "not logged at receipt". S-04 may refer to an issue that exists nowhere. CS L
A-18 Who owns site master data (addresses, relocations)? Unknown; the design routes corrections to a named "master data owner" role to be confirmed (likely Ops or Finance). S-02 closure requires the site record to be fixed. Product Lead M
A-19 Who is Finance's escalation contact? Finance has a team lead or manager who can be named as the escalation contact. Billing handoffs need an escalation target (C-04). Finance L
A-20 Can an SE be sent to a site within 24 h, outside the planned route? Yes, in most cities. Basis of the 24 h Hygiene-Critical target. X1 resolution target. Ops City Managers H — if not, X1 must vary by city
A-21 Can a visit be evidenced (photo / SPOC sign-off) from the field? Yes, via the SE mobile view [A-05]. Operational resolution evidence. Ops M — fallback: SPOC confirmation only

Open questions for the candidate (not PadCare)

Tracked in project_plan.md → "Questions for you".

00_phase0/decision_log.md

Decision Log

Format: decision · options considered · choice and why · trade-off · status. Status: Proposed (AI-drafted, candidate not yet confirmed) · Confirmed (candidate agreed) · Revised · Rejected.

Every Confirmed decision must be one the candidate can defend unaided in the 30–45 min walkthrough.

ID Decision Options considered Choice and why Trade-off Status
D-01 How to build the submission (a) One-shot generation; (b) Phased with review gates (b) The brief evaluates reasoning, and the candidate is probed on decisions in a live walkthrough. Slower Confirmed (master prompt)
D-02 Where to store the work (a) Repo root; (b) Separate folder (b) padcare-assessment/. The repo already contains an unrelated app (CEMS). None Proposed
D-03 Commit the assessment PDF? (a) Yes; (b) No (b) It is PadCare's material, and the repo's visibility is unknown. Requirements are extracted into requirements_matrix.md instead. Source must be re-uploaded for future sessions Proposed
D-04 Severity naming (a) P1/P2/P3 or Critical/High/Low; (b) Named, PadCare-specific impact levels (b) The brief explicitly lists "P1/P2/P3 tiers" under What works against you. Levels will be named by impact (e.g., hygiene risk vs service gap) and defined by observable rules. Slightly less familiar to engineers; needs a definition table Proposed
D-05 Final document scope vs master-prompt working files (a) Put everything in the doc; (b) Working files are deep, doc stays tight (b) The brief says "Quality over volume" and penalises padding. The data model, analytics spec and traceability support the doc but are condensed or omitted. Some good work is not visible to the reviewer; it can be shown in the interview Proposed
D-06 Umbrella term for what enters the register (a) Everything is a "complaint"; (b) Neutral umbrella ("Case") with types (b) "Case", with 4 case types. Calling everything a "complaint" is the root of Challenge 3, and it would inflate complaint metrics with status checks and requests. The module keeps the brief's name ("Complaint Management"). See D-10. Teams must learn one new word; may look like overreach — explain in the doc Proposed (Phase 1)
D-07 Task 2 complaint selection (a) S-01 + S-02; (b) S-02 + S-05; (c) S-01 + S-05 (a) Covers the two most common handoff chains (CS→SE/Ops and CS→Finance→CS). S-05 (KAM flow) gets less depth; covered in the classification matrix Confirmed (defaults accepted)
D-08 Test cases (Task 3) are written for which complaint? S-02 or the other Task 2 pick S-02 — billing has the richest validations (invoice ref, site relocation, routing to Finance). — Proposed
D-09 Channel integration in v1 (a) Integrate WhatsApp/email; (b) Manual logging by receiver (b) No integration is evidenced in the brief [A-04]. Process discipline first; integration later. Logging effort for CS/SE; depends on adoption Proposed
D-10 Record model (a) Everything is a complaint with a type field; (b) 4 case types + status enquiries attached to an existing case; (c) 5 case types incl. status enquiry (b) A status enquiry has no work of its own, so making it a case inflates volume and creates something that can be falsely "closed" (C-05). Attaching it keeps it countable (C-07). Intake must find the parent; if none exists, the logger must create the underlying case (lost-complaint path) Proposed (Phase 1)
D-11 Additional case types Compliment, safety incident, info query, invalid None added. Safety = highest-severity operational complaint (keeps hygiene data together); info query = service request sub-category; invalid = closure reason. Safety incidents are not visually separate; rely on severity Proposed (Phase 1)
D-12 Classification method (a) Pick from a flat list; (b) Ordered decision questions (b) Order resolves the sample traps: status first (S-04), account second (S-05), billing third (S-02), failure vs new request last (S-01 vs S-03). Slightly slower for the logger; can be a guided picker in the form Proposed (Phase 1)
D-13 Mixed messages (S-03) (a) One case, primary type only; (b) Split only independent needs into linked cases; (c) Always split per sentence (b) Independent needs have different owners and closure conditions; dependent needs (e.g., a credit note if a miss is confirmed) stay as actions inside the primary case. Linked cases add admin; the "independent" judgement needs examples in training Proposed (Phase 1)
D-14 Repeats Auto-merge vs suggest Suggest; a person decides between status enquiry / duplicate / recurrence / unrelated. Auto-merge would hide recurrences, which are the C-02 signal. Depends on logger judgement; decisions are logged Proposed (Phase 1)
D-15 Intake depth (a) Full form at first contact; (b) Two steps: Log (minimum fields, by the receiver) → Triage (complete, by CS) (b) If logging is slower than a WhatsApp reply, people won't log, and C-01 returns. A record is briefly incomplete; Triage SLA must be short (Phase 2) Proposed (Phase 1)
D-16 Owner model One owner vs resolution owner + communication owner Both fields. Resolution owner changes on handoff (C-04); the communication owner (CS) stays stable, so the customer has one voice (C-07). Still one accountable resolution owner at a time. Two fields to explain; risk of each assuming the other updates the customer → rule: the communication owner always sends updates Proposed (Phase 1)
D-17 Severity scope Severity on all types vs not on service requests Not on service requests: they have a requested-by date. A current impact becomes a linked operational complaint (S-03). Requests with real urgency rely on the linked complaint Proposed (Phase 1)
D-18 S-02 closure Corrected invoice only vs invoice + master data Both. Otherwise the October invoice repeats the error. Needs an owner for site master data (unknown) Proposed (Phase 1)
D-19 Severity levels Generic tiers vs impact-named levels Hygiene-Critical / Service-Impacting / Low-Impact, each with an observable test, plus three escalators (recurrence, 3+ sites, overdue ≥ 3 days). The system proposes, CS confirms, and a downgrade from Hygiene-Critical is visible to the Ops City Manager. Seniority, tone and revenue are not inputs (C-08). Three levels are coarse; thresholds need calibration with real data Proposed (Phase 2)
D-20 Priority Separate manual priority tiers vs a computed queue order Computed order: severity → SLA state → flags (rejected, chased, recurrence) → age. Expedite flag only with a reason, and its use is reported. Less manual control; the Expedite flag could be abused, but it is visible Proposed (Phase 2)
D-21 Ownership during a handoff Transfers on assignment vs on acceptance On acceptance. The sender stays accountable until the receiver accepts or returns it. No ownerless gap; time in Assigned is measurable (C-04). Senders carry responsibility for slow receivers; mitigated by escalation Proposed (Phase 2)
D-22 Escalation on breach Auto-reassign vs required decision The escalation contact must record a decision (reassign / take over / new date with reason). Auto-reassignment just moves the problem. Relies on managers acting; their decision time is itself measured Proposed (Phase 2)
D-23 Customer visibility without a portal Portal vs CS-driven updates CS updates at defined points plus a "maximum silence" timer (R6) per severity. A portal is deferred (A-06). CS effort; depends on discipline, so R6 breaches are tracked Proposed (Phase 2)
D-24 Non-response at confirmation Keep open vs auto-close Two reminders, then Closed – No Response at 5 business days, excluded from the confirmed-closure rate; 14-day reopen window. Some unresolved issues close silently; the reopen window and the SE-confirmation option limit this Proposed (Phase 2)
D-25 SLA clock start Logged at vs received at Received at. Logging delay counts against PadCare and stays visible (C-01). Received time is entered by the logger, so it can be wrong; backdating is allowed but audited Proposed (Phase 2)
D-26 Clock pauses Pause for internal waits vs customer only Customer only (On Hold – Customer). Internal waits are exactly what C-04 must expose. Teams may feel targets are unfair when another team is slow; the handoff data shows where time went Proposed (Phase 2)
D-27 Status list Prompt's 6 statuses incl. "Under Triage" vs leaner New · Assigned · In Progress · On Hold – Customer · Awaiting Confirmation · Closed (with reason). "Under Triage" is dropped because triage is a short action by one person and is measured by timestamp; reopen is an event, not a status. Slightly less granular status reporting Proposed (Phase 2)
D-28 How to present walkthrough findings (a) Silently fix earlier phases; (b) Show the run with ⚠ markers, list fixes, update Task 1 marked † (b) The brief rewards catching flaws ("self-critique is gold") and demands consistency. Showing both the discovery and the corrected design gives both. The document carries † markers the reader must follow Proposed (Phase 4)
D-29 Linked tasks (F-3) Handoff only vs handoff + tasks Add tasks. Hand off when the next decision belongs to another team; create a task when only a piece of work does. Mandatory tasks block resolution. One more concept; risk of using tasks to avoid real handoffs Proposed (Phase 4)
D-30 Hygiene-Critical operational routing (F-4) SE owner vs Ops City Manager owner + SE task Ops City Manager owns Hygiene-Critical cases, because SEs in the field cannot reliably accept within 1 h. Lower severities stay with the scheduled SE. More load on Ops City Managers; validate volume per city Proposed (Phase 4)
D-31 Billing severity (F-1) Amount-based vs "can the customer act on it" Customer can't process it, or the amount is wrong → Service-Impacting; cosmetic → Low-Impact. Removes the ambiguity S-02 exposed. Requires CS to ask the question Proposed (Phase 4)
D-32 On-site sign-off (F-5) Always ask via CS vs accept the SPOC/reporter sign-off Accept the sign-off from the reporter or SPOC as confirmation; anyone else's still needs CS to ask. Relies on the SE app capturing who signed [A-21] Proposed (Phase 4)
D-33 When fields are required Everything at Log vs graded L / T / H Graded: Log needs only identity, customer, reporter and words; type-specific fields are required to complete Triage; checklists are required before a handoff. Keeps logging fast (C-1) while guaranteeing complete data before work moves. Some records are briefly incomplete; the R2 timer exposes stalled triage Proposed (Phase 5)
D-34 Unmatched customer Block vs placeholder Placeholder; Triage blocked until matched. Reverses the Phase 2 "block" rule, which would lose issues from new or misspelled customers. Temporary unmatched records in the queue Proposed (Phase 5)
D-35 Validation strength Errors everywhere vs error / soft block / warning Hard errors only for what can't be fixed later without harm (wrong customer–site pair, missing Finance data at handoff, closure without evidence). Judgement calls (duplicate, recurrence, move date after the invoice month) are soft blocks or warnings. Relies on people reading warnings; soft blocks force an explicit choice Proposed (Phase 5)
D-36 Reporter role field Omit vs capture Capture for communication; explicitly excluded from severity and priority, with help text saying so (C-8). Someone could still be influenced by seeing it; overrides are reported Proposed (Phase 5)
D-37 Test case selection (6 in the doc) Many shallow tests vs 6 multi-step tests 6 multi-step tests covering the master prompt's six must-haves; each asserts the exact status, owner and rule. 5 extra cases are kept as a working set. Long rows; condense the wording in the doc Proposed (Phase 6)
D-38 Billing severity cap (F-12) Same escalators for all types vs a billing cap Billing max = Service-Impacting; recurrence escalates instead. One special case in the severity rules Proposed (Phase 6)
D-39 History storage Separate assignment / status / SLA / communication tables vs one event log One append-only CaseEvent log with typed events. One source for every metric and the audit trail; fewer tables to build. Reports filter by event type; may need materialised views at scale Proposed (Phase 7)
D-40 Metric conventions Mean vs median/P90; counting status checks Median + P90; volumes by received_at; status enquiries never counted as complaints; no-response closures reported separately. Less familiar to some readers than averages Proposed (Phase 7)
D-41 Escalator scope (AU-03) All types vs operational only Operational only. Severity keeps meaning "impact at a site"; billing and account-level concerns use their own rules. Three slightly different rules to explain Proposed (Phase 8)
D-42 Repeat terminology (AU-04) One word for both vs two levels Repeat (2nd case onwards: link + count; M3) vs Recurrence flag (3rd case onwards: escalator + root cause). Two terms to learn Proposed (Phase 8)

01_phase1/problem_definition.md

Phase 1 — Problem Definition and System Boundary

Tags: [A-xx] = assumption (see 00_phase0/assumptions_register.md), [D-xx] = decision (see decision_log.md), C-x = brief challenge, S-x = sample complaint.

1. The business problem (one paragraph)

PadCare delivers ~40,000 services a month to 2,000+ sites in 24+ cities. Customer issues arrive through six informal channels and live in individual people's WhatsApp chats, inboxes and memories. As a result, PadCare cannot reliably answer four basic questions about any issue: Did we receive it? Who owns it right now? Is it actually fixed? Has this happened before? Across all issues, it cannot answer a fifth: Where are we failing most? The module must make every customer issue a record with one owner, a type-appropriate path to a verified outcome, and structured data. It must do this without slowing down the people who receive the issues.

2. Root causes behind the 8 challenges

The 8 challenges collapse into four root causes. The design targets the causes, not the symptoms.

Root cause Challenges Design response (detailed in later phases)
R1. The issue lives with a person, not in a system C-01, C-04, C-07 Central register; the receiver must log it; a team-visible queue; tracked handoffs
R2. Every interaction is called a "complaint" C-03, C-05, C-06 Record types with their own owner, workflow and closure evidence (this phase)
R3. No memory of history C-02, C-06 Related-record search at intake; customer/site/category on every record
R4. No shared definition of "serious" or "done" C-05, C-08 Severity based on impact rules; closure confirmed by the customer

3. Users

User Interaction with the module What they need from it
CS (primary) Logs most issues, triages, owns customer communication Fast logging; one queue; full history of the customer/site; prompts for when to update the customer
SE Logs on-site verbal complaints [A-05]; executes visits and corrective actions Quick log from the field; clear task with due date; way to attach proof
Ops City Manager Receives operational escalations; owns city-level performance View of escalated and overdue items in their city; repeat hotspots
KAM Logs escalations they receive; owns account-level concerns Account-wide view across sites and cities
Finance Investigates billing complaints; issues corrections/credit notes [A-11] Clear handoff with invoice details attached; due date
Client SPOC / End User (indirect) Raise issues; confirm resolution Acknowledgement, proactive updates, a reference number; asked "is it fixed?" before closure. No direct system access in v1 [A-06]
Leadership / Product (indirect) Consume reports Trustworthy, structured data

4. Module objectives (proposed, measurable)

Targets are proposals for validation, not PadCare commitments [A-07].

# Objective Indicator (defined fully in Phase 7) Challenge
O1 Every customer issue is in the register, regardless of channel Share of records logged from each channel; "found only on a later status enquiry" count → trend to 0 C-01
O2 Every open record has exactly one accountable owner Records without an owner = 0 (hard rule) C-04
O3 Repeat issues are visible at the moment of intake Share of repeats identified at intake vs found later C-02
O4 Interactions are separated by type Share of records reclassified after triage (lower = clearer rules) C-03
O5 Closure means the customer confirmed, or a defined no-response rule applied Reopen rate; share of records closed on confirmation C-05
O6 Issues can be analysed by city, site, customer, category and time All of these fields are structured, not free text C-06
O7 Customers stop having to chase Status enquiries per open record C-07
O8 Severity follows impact rules, not who is asking Severity overrides logged with a reason; reporter seniority is not an input C-08

5. System boundary

In scope — version 1

Area v1 scope
Register One central register of Cases in PadCareOne [D-10]
Intake Manual logging by the PadCare employee who receives the issue, from any of the 6 channels [D-09]. Logging happens in two steps: a fast Log step, then a Triage step that completes the record [D-15]
Classification 4 case types + status enquiries attached to existing cases (see classification_matrix.md)
Related records Search for and suggest related cases (same customer/site/category/time window); links between cases. No automatic merging
Severity and priority Rule-based, impact-led; defined in Phase 2
Ownership One accountable owner; tracked handoffs with acknowledgement; escalation timers
Lifecycle Statuses, closure evidence by type, customer confirmation, reopening
Customer communication CS sends updates through the customer's existing channel; every update is logged on the case
Reporting Structured fields and status/owner history sufficient for core metrics; a basic list/report view

Out of scope — deferred or external

Item Why When
WhatsApp / email / telephony integration No evidence it exists [A-04]; v1 proves the process first v2 — automatic capture from the support inbox first (highest volume per effort, assumed)
Customer self-service portal / tracking link PadCareOne is internal [A-06] v2 — read-only status link by case reference
Invoice generation / credit-note issuing Finance's existing process, whatever it is [A-03]; the module records the outcome and reference Integration later
Field scheduling / dispatch Assumed to exist in PadCareOne [A-02]; the module creates or links a visit request, it does not replace scheduling —
Commercial negotiation content (pricing, contract terms) Captured as an account-level case so it is visible, but the negotiation itself happens outside —
Automatic classification (NLP/AI), sentiment Needs labelled history first, which v1 creates v3
Compliments / general feedback Not in the brief's problem set Later, if wanted

6. Design principles carried into all phases

  1. Classify by what the customer needs PadCare to do, not by the words used (S-03, S-04, S-05 all use "complaint" words but need different responses).
  2. One case per independent customer need, not per message. A message can create 0 cases (a pure status enquiry), 1, or several linked cases.
  3. Logging must be faster than not logging. Only the minimum is mandatory at Log; the rest is completed at Triage. A heavy intake form would push CS back to WhatsApp, which recreates C-01.
  4. The system suggests and a person decides — for repeats, duplicates and severity overrides. Every override needs a reason.
  5. Two owner roles per case: the resolution owner (whoever must act now; this changes on handoff) and the communication owner (CS for the customer; stable). This separates C-04 handoffs from C-07 customer contact.
  6. "Done" is defined per type by evidence, not by a reply to the customer.

7. Known risks

Risk Likelihood Mitigation
CS/SE don't log issues received informally (adoption) High Two-step intake; KAM and SE can log; a lost issue that surfaces later via a status enquiry is flagged and counted (makes the gap visible)
Misclassification at Log Medium Type can be changed at Triage with a reason; reclassification rate tracked
Customers don't confirm closure High Defined non-response rule (Phase 2) rather than leaving cases open forever
Master data is wrong (e.g., S-02 relocated site) Medium "Site not found / site changed" exception path; corrections routed to whoever owns master data
Over-engineering for v1 Medium Out-of-scope table above; Phase 8 audit for anything nobody would use
Severity rules are gamed or ignored Medium Overrides need a reason and are reported

8. Unresolved questions (for PadCare)

# Question Why it matters Current assumption
U-1 Does PadCareOne hold customer, site and service schedule records? Validation and visit linking Yes [A-01] [A-02]
U-2 Is every account assigned a named CS owner? Is there a CS team lead? Auto-assignment; cover during leave Named CS owner yes [A-09]; a CS Lead role is not in the brief, so it is not relied on [A-15]
U-3 Who owns an account-level concern when the account has no KAM? S-05 routing Ops City Manager of the account's primary city [A-10] [A-15]
U-4 Does an additional unit (S-03) change the customer's charges or contract? Whether a service request needs commercial approval Possibly; the design allows an approval step [A-16]
U-5 What is the normal service frequency by site type? Hygiene severity threshold for missed collections Varies, at least monthly at some sites [A-08]
U-6 Complaints raised before go-live — migrate or not? S-04-type enquiries about issues that were never logged Not migrated; created on demand when chased [A-17]
01_phase1/classification_matrix.md

Phase 1 — Classification Matrix

1. Record model [D-10] [D-11]

Everything logged becomes a Case of one of four types. A status enquiry is not a case: it is logged as a follow-up entry on the case it refers to.

Case type Definition (one test) Typical sub-categories (v1, extendable) Default resolution owner Communication owner "Resolved" means (evidence)
Operational complaint PadCare did not deliver, or delivered badly, something it already committed to Missed collection/service · Late service · Unit not cleaned/odour · Unit overflowing · Unit damaged/missing · SE conduct · Other CS triages → Ops City Manager (Hygiene-Critical, with an SE visit task) or the site's scheduled SE (other severities); Ops City Manager on escalation (Phase 2 v1.1, F-4) CS Corrective action done and verified: visit completed and recorded, with proof (e.g., photo or SPOC sign-off) [A-02]
Billing complaint Disagreement with an invoice, charge, payment or credit Wrong amount · Wrong site/address · Charged for service not delivered · Duplicate invoice · Credit note pending · Other CS triages → Finance investigates → back to CS CS Corrected invoice(s) — all affected invoices — or a credit note issued (references recorded), or a documented explanation; plus any master-data task completed (F-8, D-18)
Service request Customer asks for something new or changed relative to what is agreed; nothing has failed Additional unit · Remove/relocate unit · Change schedule · Extra/one-off visit · Site details change · Document request CS → Ops City Manager (fulfilment); KAM approval if commercial terms change [A-16] CS Request fulfilled (e.g., installation completed and recorded) or formally declined with a reason
Account-level concern Customer wants a relationship-level response (review, meeting, commercial change), or describes a trend across sites rather than one incident to fix Service quality trend · Multi-site issue · Commercial / pricing · Contract / renewal · Relationship escalation KAM; if no KAM → Ops City Manager of the primary city [A-10] [A-15] CS (KAM may communicate directly) Agreed action plan recorded, with a named owner and review date; customer agrees the plan
Status enquiry (not a case) Customer asks about the progress of an issue already raised — Communication owner of the parent case CS Update sent and logged. Never closes the parent case

Severity applies to operational complaints, billing complaints and account-level concerns. Service requests have a requested-by date, not a severity. If the request carries a current impact, that impact becomes a linked operational complaint (see S-03). Severity levels and rules are defined in 02_phase2/end_to_end_flow.md §2.5.

Additional types evaluated and rejected

Candidate Decision Why
Compliment / feedback Not in v1 Not part of the brief's problem; adds a type nobody owns
Safety / health incident Not a separate type It is an operational complaint at the highest severity; a separate type would split the hygiene data (C-06)
Information / how-to query Sub-category of service request ("Document / information request") Low volume (assumed), same owner as a service request
Invalid / not for PadCare Not a type; a closure reason ("Cancelled — invalid / not PadCare") Something has to be logged before it can be judged invalid

2. Classification decision table (asked in this order) [D-12]

The order matters: each question catches a sample complaint that a later question would misclassify.

Step Question to the logger If YES What the step protects against
1 Is the customer asking about an issue they already raised? Status enquiry. Search for the parent case → attach a follow-up (see §4) S-04 mentions "missed service"; without this step it becomes a duplicate operational complaint
2 Is the customer asking for an account-level response (meeting, review, commercial change), or describing a trend across sites with no single incident to fix? Account-level concern S-05 mentions "service quality"; without this step it becomes a vague operational complaint with nothing to fix
3 Is it about an invoice, charge, payment or credit? Billing complaint S-02 mentions a site move; without this step it may be logged as a "site details change" service request and Finance never sees it
4 Is the customer asking PadCare to fix or make up for something already committed (missed, late, poor, broken, conduct)? Operational complaint —
5 Is the customer asking for something new or changed? Service request S-03 is a request, not a failure (the brief: "a service request in disguise")
6 (always) Split check: does the message contain a second need that is independent (could be resolved on its own) and needs a different owner or closure condition? Create a second case and link them S-03: overflow relief ≠ new unit installation

Split rule detail. Independent needs become separate linked cases. Dependent needs become actions inside the primary case.

  • Example of a dependent need: "service was missed and you charged us for it". This is one operational complaint, with a Finance credit-note action if the miss is confirmed. The billing outcome depends on the operational finding.

3. The five sample complaints

S-01 Missed collection S-02 Invoice, relocated site S-03 Additional unit S-04 "Has my complaint been resolved?" S-05 Quality drop, multiple sites
Decided at step 4 3 5 (+6 split) 1 2
Case type Operational complaint Billing complaint Service request + linked operational complaint Status enquiry → follow-up on the parent case Account-level concern
Sub-category Missed collection Wrong site/address (triage may change this to "Charged for service not delivered", see below) SR: Additional unit · OC: Unit overflowing — (parent: Missed collection) Service quality trend
What the customer needs A collection visit now Corrected invoice (a) New unit on 4th floor; (b) overflow stopped now An update, and the original issue fixed A meeting and a credible improvement plan
Impact signals (inputs to severity, Phase 2) Collection overdue against schedule; customer reports a hygiene risk (to be verified, not taken from the wording, C-08) Financial; no hygiene impact Daily overflow = current hygiene exposure at one location Customer already chased once; no update was given Multiple sites; quality trend; relationship risk
Severity (Phase 2 rules) Hygiene-Critical if units are full or the collection is ≥ 3 days overdue; else Service-Impacting. The customer's wording is not used on its own Service-Impacting (billed incorrectly; no hygiene exposure) OC: Hygiene-Critical (overflow = current exposure) · SR: none (committed date instead) Inherits the parent's; priority raised by the "customer chased" flag Highest severity among the account's open cases; else Service-Impacting (quality trend)
Resolution owner path CS → Ops City Manager (Hygiene-Critical) → SE visit task → CS CS → Finance → CS SR: CS → Ops City Manager (+ KAM if commercial) [A-16] · OC: CS → Ops City Manager (Hygiene-Critical) → SE task for an interim extra collection Parent case's current owner; CS replies KAM (or Ops City Manager if no KAM)
Closure evidence Visit recorded as completed + proof; customer confirms Corrected invoice/credit note reference and site record corrected so next month's invoice is right; customer confirms SR: installation recorded; OC: overflow controlled (interim + capacity fixed); each confirmed separately Update sent and logged; the parent case stays open Action plan agreed + review date; customer agrees
Repeat check Missed collections at this site in the look-back window Billing complaints for this account/site; likely to recur monthly until the site record is fixed Earlier overflow complaints at this site (may show under-capacity) Is the repeat lookup: find the parent Pull all cases across the account's sites; the evidence base for the meeting
Triage question to resolve Was the visit scheduled? Does the system show it as done? (If "done" but not collected → a data-integrity / SE issue, investigate) Address only (re-issue invoice), or charges for a site no longer occupied (credit note + check whether services were really performed July–Sept)? Does the extra unit change charges (needs approval)? Is the existing schedule being met? Does the parent exist? Is it open? Was it closed without confirmation? Does the account have a KAM? Which sites and cities?

Notes the walkthroughs (Phase 4) must test

  • S-02 hides a master-data problem. If the site record still holds the old address, every future invoice will be wrong. That would generate a repeat billing complaint each month. Closure must require the site record to be corrected, not just the September invoice. Who owns site master data is unknown; validate with PadCare.
  • S-03's two cases close separately. The complaint can close once overflow is controlled, even if installation takes weeks. If they were one case, either the overflow waits for the installation, or the case closes before the installation happens.
  • S-04 is evidence of a design failure, not a new issue. It means the customer was not updated. It should count against update performance (C-07), and it may expose a complaint that was never logged (C-01).
  • S-05 should spawn child cases. If the meeting surfaces specific failing sites, each becomes an operational complaint linked to the account concern, so each one is actually fixed.

4. Status enquiry handling (S-04 pattern)

Situation found on search Action Data recorded
Parent found, open Attach a follow-up; CS sends an update within the acknowledgement SLA (Phase 2); raise the parent's priority Follow-up count +1; "customer chased" flag
Parent found, awaiting customer confirmation Treat as a confirmation conversation: ask whether it is resolved Confirmation outcome
Parent found, closed, customer says not fixed Reopen the parent (if within the reopen window) or create a new case linked as a recurrence Reopen count / recurrence link
No parent found The original was never logged (lost, C-01). Create the underlying case now, with the customer-stated original report date and a "not logged at receipt" flag Lost-complaint indicator for O1

5. Distinguishing status enquiry vs duplicate vs recurrence [D-14]

Situation Test Handling
Status enquiry Same issue, customer asking for progress Follow-up on the parent, no new case
Duplicate Same incident logged twice (e.g., SPOC on WhatsApp and an End User by email) Second record is closed as "Duplicate of #…", linked; its contact details are added to the parent
Recurrence Same customer + site + category, but the earlier case was resolved and the issue happened again New case, linked as a recurrence; repeat count shown; feeds severity/escalation (Phase 2)
Related but different Same site, different category Shown as context only; no link required

6. Ambiguity test (are the rules unambiguous?)

New, made-up messages run through the decision table to check the rules hold up.

# Test message Step Result Rules held?
T1 "The bin wasn't cleaned last week and you still charged us." 4 Operational complaint; credit note as a dependent action (split rule) Yes
T2 "Please move the unit from the 2nd to the 3rd floor." 5 Service request: relocate unit Yes
T3 "Any update on the extra bin we asked for?" 1 Status enquiry on a service request parent Yes — status enquiries apply to all types
T4 "Three of our sites missed collection this week." 4 Three operational complaints (one per site) Partly. Is it also an account concern? Rule: only if the customer asks for an account-level response. Each site still needs fixing → per-site cases. If KAM involvement is wanted, link them to an account concern. Watch in Phase 4
T5 "We'd like to reduce the price for next year." 2 Account concern: commercial Yes
T6 "Your SE was rude to our staff." 4 Operational complaint: SE conduct Yes. Severity rules must cover non-hygiene impact (Phase 2)
T7 "The odour is back again." 4 Operational complaint; the repeat check finds earlier odour cases → recurrence Yes
T8 End User emails directly; the SPOC also WhatsApps the same issue 4 First = case; second = duplicate, linked Yes, depends on the duplicate check at Log
T9 "Can you send a copy of the August invoice?" 5 Service request: document request (not a billing complaint, as nothing is disputed) Yes
T10 Customer complains about a site that is not theirs in the master data — Not a type question: a customer–site validation exception (Phase 5) Out of classification scope

Result: 9 of 10 classify cleanly. T4 (multi-site, specific incidents) is the one grey area. The tie-break rule is written above and flagged for the Phase 4 stress test.

02_phase2/end_to_end_flow.md

Detailed flow diagram (complaint_lifecycle.mmd)

Phase 2 — End-to-End Process Design

Revision: v1.1 — walkthrough fixes F-1…F-8, F-10 applied (marked †; see 04_phase4/design_review.md).

Diagram: complaint_lifecycle.mmd (rendered: complaint_lifecycle.png). SLA targets: sla_matrix.md. Case types and the classification order come from 01_phase1/classification_matrix.md and are reused unchanged. All rules here are proposals for validation with PadCare [A-07].

0. The process at a glance

Stage Steps Who Status after the stage Main challenge(s) addressed
ST1 Intake 1.1 Receive · 1.2 Log · 1.3 Validate customer and site Whoever receives the issue New C-01
ST2 Triage 2.1 Related-record search · 2.2 Classify · 2.3 Duplicate / split check · 2.4 Recurrence check · 2.5 Severity · 2.6 Acknowledge the customer CS (communication owner) New → Assigned C-02, C-03, C-08, C-07
ST3 Route and assign 3.1 Route by type · 3.2 Handoff protocol (incl. accept / return) · 3.3 Linked tasks · 3.4 Statuses during routing CS → receiving owner Assigned → In Progress C-04
ST4 Resolve 4.1 Investigate and act · 4.2 Further handoffs · 4.3 Escalate on timers or events · 4.4 Record resolution evidence Resolution owner In Progress (On Hold – Customer allowed) C-04, C-05
ST5 Verify and close 5.1 Share the resolution, request confirmation · 5.2 Confirm / reject / no response · 5.3 Close · 5.4 Reopen or recurrence CS Awaiting Confirmation → Closed C-05, C-07
ST6 Learn (continuous) Every step writes a timestamped event System — C-06

ST1 — Intake

1.1 Who logs, by channel

Rule: whoever at PadCare receives the issue logs it in PadCareOne. Forwarding to someone else does not count as logging.

Channel (brief) Who logs When (target, see SLA R1) Notes
WhatsApp from SPOC to their CS contact That CS person Within 2 business hours of receipt Screenshot attached as evidence (optional)
Email to the generic support inbox CS on inbox duty (rota) [A-09] Within 2 business hours Email text pasted; email subject kept as reference
Phone call to CS CS who took the call During or straight after the call —
Raised during a CS check-in call CS making the call Straight after the call One check-in call can produce several cases (split rule)
Escalation from KAM after a difficult client interaction KAM logs it (no forwarding emails) Same business day Reporter = the client person who raised it. Their seniority is recorded as a contact role only; it is not an input to severity (C-08)
Verbal report to an SE on site SE, using a quick log on mobile [A-05] Before leaving the site Fallback if there is no mobile access: SE calls CS, and CS logs it with channel = "SE on site"

1.2 Log — minimum fields (fast step)

The Log step is meant to take about 2 minutes. Everything else is completed at Triage [D-15]. Mandatory at Log: customer account, site (optional for account-level concerns), reporter (name, contact, role), channel, date/time received (defaults to now and can be backdated), customer's words (verbatim), and the logger's best-guess type. Full field specification: Phase 5.

If CS already replied informally before logging (e.g., "checking" on WhatsApp), the logger records "customer already acknowledged at [time]". This is kept as a customer update, but only an acknowledgement that includes a case reference counts towards R3 † (F-10).

On save:

  • Case ID generated.
  • Status New.
  • Resolution owner = the account's named CS owner [A-09]. If that person is marked unavailable (leave), the city CS queue owns it.

A case is never ownerless, even at New. This is the direct fix for C-01's "if that person is on leave, it's gone".

1.3 Validate customer and site

Result Handling Type
Customer and site found, and the site belongs to the customer Continue —
Site not found / the customer says the site moved (S-02) Log with an "Unverified site" flag. CS resolves it at Triage: pick the correct site, or request a master-data correction [A-18] Warning (does not block logging)
Site belongs to a different customer Block; choose the right customer or site Hard error
Customer not found Log against an "Unmatched customer" placeholder with the name as stated; Triage cannot complete until matched † (Phase 5 review: blocking here would lose the issue, C-1) Warning at Log; hard error at Triage

Why the site flag is only a warning: blocking at Log would mean the issue never gets recorded (C-01). Data quality is fixed one step later, at Triage.

ST2 — Triage (CS)

2.1 Related-record search (automatic, shown before classification)

On opening a New case, the system shows:

  • Open cases at this site (any type);
  • Cases at this site in the last 90 days with the same category (any status);
  • For the account: open account-level concerns and open cases at other sites of the account.

2.2 Classify

Use the ordered questions from Phase 1:

  1. Is the customer asking about an issue they already raised? → status enquiry
  2. Do they want an account-level response, or report a trend across sites? → account-level concern
  3. Is it about an invoice, charge, payment or credit? → billing complaint
  4. Do they want PadCare to fix something it already committed to? → operational complaint
  5. Is it a new or changed request? → service request

Then set the sub-category.

  • Status enquiry branch: a follow-up is added to the parent case, and its priority is raised (flag "customer chased"). CS sends an update within the acknowledgement target. No new case is created.
    • If the parent is closed, the reopen rules in §5.4 apply.
    • If no parent exists, the underlying case is created with the customer-stated report date and the flag "Not logged at receipt". This counts against C-01.

2.3 Duplicate and split check

  • Duplicate (same incident already open): the new record closes as Closed – Cancelled – Duplicate and is linked to the parent. The new reporter is added as a contact on the parent.
  • Split (a second independent need with a different owner or closure condition, e.g., S-03): a linked case is created.

2.4 Recurrence check

† (audit AU-04) Two levels, so "repeat" means one thing:

  • Repeat (from the 2nd case): any earlier case at the same site with the same sub-category within 90 days is suggested as a Recurrence of link, and the repeat count is shown. This feeds metric M3.
  • Recurrence flag (from the 3rd case, i.e. ≥ 2 earlier**):** the case is marked Recurrence (n-th):
    • the count is shown to everyone handling it;
    • the severity escalator applies (2.5) for operational complaints; billing escalates instead (F-12);
    • a mandatory root-cause note is required at resolution.

This turns "the third bad-odour complaint" (C-02) into a visible, rule-driven event.

2.5 Severity (impact-based) and priority

Severity levels [D-04]. Applies to operational complaints, billing complaints and account-level concerns. Service requests have a requested-by date instead [D-17].

Level Definition (observable test) Examples from the brief
Hygiene-Critical A hygiene or health exposure exists at the site now: waste uncollected beyond schedule with units full, overflowing units, a damaged or leaking unit, contamination S-01 (if units are full or overdue), the overflow half of S-03
Service-Impacting PadCare failed an agreed service, without a current hygiene exposure; or an invoice the customer cannot act on: wrong amount, or wrong entity/site/address that stops them processing it † (F-1) Late visit with units not yet full, unit not cleaned properly, SE conduct, S-02
Low-Impact No service, hygiene or financial consequence Cosmetic issues; an invoice error that does not stop the customer processing it (e.g., a typo in the contact name); a commercial query with no service failure

Escalators (operational complaints only † AU-03). Each raises the level by one, capped at Hygiene-Critical:

  • Recurrence: the 3rd or later case at the site for the same category within 90 days (2.4).
  • Scope: the same issue at 3 or more sites of one customer.
  • Duration: missed collection overdue by ≥ 3 days past its scheduled date [A-08] (threshold to be validated per site type).
  • Billing cap † (F-12): billing complaints never exceed Service-Impacting (there is no hygiene exposure). A billing recurrence or a multi-site billing issue instead escalates: Finance escalation contact + KAM informed.

Who decides.

  • The system proposes a level from CS's answers to the impact questions: Is there a hygiene exposure now? How many sites/users are affected? Is the service commitment broken? (Billing:) Is the amount wrong, or can the customer not process the invoice? † Recurrence and duration are filled in automatically from history and the schedule [A-02].
  • CS confirms the level.
  • CS may raise it, with a reason.
  • Lowering Hygiene-Critical requires a reason and is visible to the Ops City Manager.
  • Reporter seniority, the customer's tone and account revenue are not inputs (C-08). The customer's wording ("it's a hygiene issue") triggers the impact question but does not set the answer.

Account-level concerns take the highest severity among the open cases at the account's sites. If there are none, they are Service-Impacting for a quality trend and Low-Impact for a commercial topic.

Priority = the order in which a queue is worked. It is computed, not chosen:

  1. Severity;
  2. SLA state (breached > at risk, meaning less than 25% of the time is left > on track);
  3. Flags: resolution rejected, customer chased, recurrence;
  4. Received time (oldest first).

A KAM or Ops City Manager can set an Expedite flag, but only with a mandatory reason. Its use is reported, so escalation by influence becomes visible rather than hidden.

2.6 Acknowledge the customer

CS sends: case reference, the type as the customer would understand it ("a missed collection complaint", "a request for an additional unit"), the next step, and when they'll hear back. The update is logged on the case.

ST3 — Route and assign

3.1 Routing by type

Case type First resolution owner after Triage Typical further handoffs Escalation contact
Operational complaint Hygiene-Critical: Ops City Manager, with the SE visit as a linked task † (F-4). Otherwise: the SE scheduled for the site [A-02], else the Ops City Manager to dispatch. CS keeps it if it can be resolved by a call (e.g., conduct explanation) SE → CS (evidence) Ops City Manager; KAM is notified for KAM accounts at Hygiene-Critical or the 3rd recurrence
Billing complaint Finance Finance → CS (outcome to communicate); Finance → master-data owner if the site record is wrong (S-02) [A-18] Finance escalation contact [A-19]; KAM notified if a KAM account
Service request Ops City Manager (fulfilment) → KAM (or CS where there is no KAM) for commercial approval if charges change [A-16] → SE (installation) Ops City Manager
Account-level concern KAM; if no KAM, the Ops City Manager of the account's primary city [A-10] Spawns linked child cases for specific site failures — (already at the top of the brief's role list)

The communication owner stays CS for every type [D-16]. CS sends all customer updates, even when Finance or an SE holds the case. The exception is account-level concerns, where the KAM may also talk to the customer directly; the updates are still logged on the case.

3.2 Handoff protocol (applies to every change of owner)

Element Rule
Sending owner / receiving owner Both recorded
Reason Mandatory, chosen from a list (e.g., "needs site visit", "invoice correction", "commercial approval", "escalation") plus free text
Required information A checklist per handoff type. CS → Finance: invoice number, invoice month, disputed line or amount, what the customer expects, customer evidence attached; for a wrong site/address, the correct address and effective date (F-7). Finance's own checklist: identify all invoices affected since the effective date † (F-8). CS → SE / Ops: site, exact location on site (e.g., 4th floor), access contact, problem, severity
Assigned at / due by Timestamped; acceptance deadline from SLA R4
Acceptance The receiver accepts (ownership transfers; status In Progress) or returns it with a reason (back to the sender, status In Progress with the sender, so the sender can complete the information or put the case On Hold – Customer † (F-2)). A return is not a rejection into nowhere
Accountability before acceptance The sender remains accountable until acceptance
No response by the deadline Escalated to the receiver's escalation contact. The sender is notified and stays accountable

3.3 Linked tasks † (F-3)

Some work by another team does not need ownership to move. Examples: the SE visit for a Hygiene-Critical case owned by the Ops City Manager; a site master-data correction needed by Finance (S-02); an installation for a service request.

These are linked tasks inside the case:

  • Fields: task owner, due date, done/not done, evidence.
  • The case owner stays accountable for the case; the task owner is accountable for the task.
  • Task acceptance and overdue escalation follow the handoff timers (R4, 4.3).
  • A mandatory task that is not done blocks resolution (4.4).

Rule of thumb: hand off when the next decision belongs to another team; create a task when only a piece of work does.

3.4 Statuses during routing

Assigned = waiting for the receiver to accept. In Progress = accepted by the current owner. Each new handoff returns the case to Assigned. This makes the "in nobody's inbox" period (C-04) visible and measurable as time spent in Assigned.

ST4 — Resolve

4.1 Investigate and act — by type

Type Typical actions Resolution evidence required before Awaiting Confirmation (system-enforced)
Operational complaint Check the schedule: was the visit scheduled? marked done? → plan the visit → SE visits → fix A visit record linked to the case and proof (photo of serviced unit or SPOC sign-off) and, for recurrences, a root-cause note and, for Missed collection, the next regular visit confirmed in the schedule † (F-6). All mandatory linked tasks done. Data-integrity flag: if the schedule shows the visit as "completed" but the customer says it wasn't, the case cannot be resolved without an Ops City Manager note
Billing complaint Finance checks the invoice against site/service records → corrects, issues a credit note, or confirms it is correct Corrected invoice no(s). (all affected invoices) or credit note no. or written explanation. Plus the master-data task completed, where the cause was master data (S-02) [D-18]
Service request Approval (if commercial) → schedule → fulfil Fulfilment record (e.g., installation done with location, date and photo) or a decline reason communicated to the customer
Account-level concern Pull the account's case history → meeting → action plan → child cases for specific failures Meeting held (date, attendees), action plan with owners and dates, review date. The customer agreeing to the plan is the confirmation

4.2 On Hold – Customer

Allowed only when PadCare is waiting on the customer (site access, a missing invoice copy, the new address). Rules:

  • the SLA clock pauses;
  • reminders go out at 2 and 4 business days;
  • after 7 business days the case is closed as Closed – No Response (after one final message).

Internal waiting (Finance, SE) can never use On Hold. That would hide exactly the delays C-04 is about.

4.3 Escalation triggers

Trigger Escalated to What they must do
Handoff not accepted by the deadline Receiver's escalation contact Accept, reassign or return, within 2 business hours (Hygiene-Critical: 1 calendar hour)
75% of the resolution SLA used Owner + CS (an "at risk" alert) Update the ETA; CS updates the customer
Resolution SLA breached Escalation contact by type (3.1) Record a decision within 4 business hours: reassign / take over / new due date with reason. Not an automatic reassignment
Recurrence (3rd+ in 90 days) Ops City Manager; KAM informed for KAM accounts Root-cause review before resolution
Resolution rejected twice by the customer Ops City Manager (operational) / Finance escalation contact (billing) / KAM Take ownership or define a new plan
Hygiene-Critical at triage Ops City Manager notified (no action required unless the visit target is at risk) —

4.4 Further handoffs

Any owner can hand off again (e.g., SE → Ops City Manager when a part is unavailable; Finance → master-data owner). The same protocol applies.

ST5 — Verify and close (CS)

5.1 Request confirmation

When resolution evidence is recorded, the case goes to Awaiting Confirmation and ownership returns to CS. CS tells the customer what was done, citing the evidence (e.g., "collection completed on 14 Oct, photo attached", "credit note CN-123 issued"), and asks: "Is this resolved for you?"

5.2 Customer response

Response Result
Confirms Closed – Confirmed
Rejects ("still overflowing") Back to In Progress with the last resolution owner. Rejection count +1; reason recorded. The SLA continues from the original receipt time, not reset. A 2nd rejection escalates (4.3)
No response Reminders at 2 and 4 business days; Closed – No Response at 5 business days. This closure is excluded from the "customer-confirmed" rate (C-05 metric)
Reporter or SPOC signed off on site in the SE app (operational) † (F-5) Counts as confirmation → Closed – Confirmed on site. CS sends a closure note, not a question. A sign-off by anyone else (e.g., security staff) still needs the CS request
Customer unreachable but the SE confirms on the next visit (operational only) May be recorded as confirmation with the SE as the confirmer. Shown separately in reporting

5.3 Closure rules

  • Only CS (communication owner) can close, except: duplicates/invalid (any triager, with a reason) and account-level concerns (KAM).
  • Closure needs: a closure reason and resolution evidence (enforced) and a confirmation outcome.
  • Answering a status enquiry never changes the parent's status (C-05, S-04).

5.4 Reopen vs recurrence

When the issue comes back Handling
Within 14 calendar days of closure, same issue Reopen the case → In Progress; reopen count +1; original owner; SLA restarts from the reopen time
After 14 days, or a new incident of the same category New case, linked as a recurrence (2.4)
Closed as Duplicate or Invalid, then found to be valid Reopen with a reason (any CS)

ST6 — Learn: events written by the process

Every event row = case ID, event, actor, role, timestamp, old/new value. This is the raw material for Phase 7 metrics (C-06).

Event Written at Used for
case_logged (with channel, received_at, logged_at) 1.2 Volume by channel, registration delay, C-01
site_flagged_unverified 1.3 Master data quality
followup_received 2.2 Status enquiries per case (C-07)
classified / reclassified 2.2 Category mix (C-06), classification accuracy (C-03)
linked (duplicate / recurrence / split / child) 2.3–2.4 Repeat rate (C-02)
severity_set / severity_overridden (with reason) 2.5 Override rate (C-08)
customer_update_sent 2.6, 4.x, 5.1 First response time, silence gaps (C-07)
handoff_initiated / handoff_accepted / handoff_returned 3.2 Time in Assigned, return rate (C-04)
status_changed (incl. hold start/end) All Ageing, SLA clocks
escalated (trigger, to whom, decision) 4.3 Escalation rate
task_created / task_done (owner, due) 3.3 Task ageing by team (C-04)
resolution_recorded (evidence type) 4.4 Time to resolution
confirmation_requested / confirmed / rejected / no_response 5.x Confirmation rate, rejection rate (C-05)
closed (reason) / reopened 5.3–5.4 Reopen rate (C-05)

Status lifecycle

Status Meaning Accountable owner Who may move it out
New Logged, not yet triaged Account CS owner (or city CS queue) CS
Assigned Handed off, not yet accepted Sender (until acceptance) Receiver (accept → In Progress with the receiver; return → In Progress with the sender); escalation contact
In Progress Owner is working on it Current resolution owner Owner; CS (for hold/closure paths)
On Hold – Customer Waiting on the customer only; clock paused CS CS; system (time-out)
Awaiting Confirmation Evidence recorded; customer asked to confirm CS CS; system (time-out)
Closed Displayed as Closed – <reason>. Closure reason (canonical list †): Confirmed · Confirmed on site · Plan Agreed (account-level) · No Response · Cancelled – Duplicate · Cancelled – Invalid (sub-reason: not a PadCare issue / logged in error / test) — CS / KAM / Ops City Manager (reopen)

Invalid transitions (system-blocked):

  • Any status → Closed – Confirmed without resolution evidence.
  • New → Awaiting Confirmation.
  • An owner other than CS/KAM closing a case.
  • Use of On Hold – Customer with a non-customer hold reason.
02_phase2/sla_matrix.md

Phase 2 — Proposed SLA Matrix

All targets are proposals [A-07]. There are no known contractual SLAs. Validate with CS, Ops and Finance before go-live, then calibrate using 2–3 months of data from the module itself.

Clock rules

  • Hygiene-Critical: calendar hours (waste accumulates at weekends too). Everything else: business hours, 09:00–18:00 Mon–Sat [A-12].
  • All clocks start at received at (when the customer told PadCare), not logged at. Late logging is therefore visible as lost time, and is not hidden.
  • Only On Hold – Customer pauses a clock. Internal waits never pause it.
  • Resolution clocks do not reset on rejection. They restart on reopen (a reopen is a new resolution attempt; reopen counts are tracked separately).

A. Response targets (how fast we react) — apply to all case types

ID Stage Measured from → to Hygiene-Critical Service-Impacting Low-Impact / Service request Why this target
R1 Registration received → logged 1 h 2 business h 2 business h (SE on site: before leaving the site) Logging is the C-01 fix; it must happen while the details are fresh. 2 h allows for a CS person on a call
R2 Triage (classified, severity set) logged → triaged 1 h 4 business h 1 business day Severity cannot be known until triage, so a short target applies to all; Hygiene-Critical is often only discovered at triage, so R2 is applied retroactively (see note)
R3 Acknowledgement to customer (case ref + next step) received → first logged update 2 h Same business day (≤ 6 business h) Next business day The customer must know it was received before they think to chase (C-07). Measured from received, so it includes R1 and R2
R4 Handoff acceptance assigned → accepted/returned 1 h 4 business h 1 business day The C-04 fix; long enough to read and accept, short enough that nothing sits for days
R5 First progress update (plan / ETA) received → update with ETA 4 h (visit time confirmed) 1 business day 2 business days Customers chase when they have no ETA, not when work is slow
R6 Maximum silence while open gap between logged customer updates 1 calendar day 2 business days 3 business days (account concern: weekly) Keeps the customer updated without a portal; S-04 ("no one has updated me") would trigger an R6 breach before the customer had to ask

Note on R2 for Hygiene-Critical: a case logged as Service-Impacting and upgraded at triage is measured against the Service-Impacting R2 target. From the upgrade onwards, Hygiene-Critical targets apply.

B. Resolution targets (how fast we fix) — by type and severity

ID Case type Hygiene-Critical Service-Impacting Low-Impact Why
X1 Operational complaint (received → resolution evidence) 24 h (corrective visit done) 3 business days 5 business days 24 h is the shortest promise that is realistic for a field visit outside the planned route [A-08]. Validate against SE capacity per city
X2 Billing complaint n/a (billing has no hygiene exposure) 5 business days 7 business days Investigation + correction + re-issue across CS → Finance → CS. Long enough for Finance to check service records; short enough to fix the invoice before the next billing cycle
X3 Service request n/a — a linked complaint carries any urgency Committed date agreed at triage (default 10 business days for an installation; 3 for a one-off extra visit) same Fulfilment depends on stock and approval; a promised date is more honest than a generic SLA. Measured as "fulfilled by the committed date"
X4 Account-level concern Meeting within 2 business days Meeting within 5 business days; action plan agreed within 10 business days Response within 5 business days Relationship issues need a fast first meeting; the plan needs data gathering (account case history)

C. Verification targets

ID Stage Target Why
V1 Confirmation request sent Within 1 business day of resolution evidence (Hygiene-Critical: same day) Ask while the fix is fresh
V2 Customer confirmation window 5 business days; reminders at day 2 and 4 → Closed – No Response Avoids cases staying open forever while keeping confirmation the default
V3 Reopen window 14 calendar days after closure Covers at least one more service cycle at frequent-service sites; after that it is a recurrence
V4 On Hold – Customer limit 7 business days, reminders at day 2 and 4 Same reasoning as V2

D. Escalation timers (from end_to_end_flow.md §4.3)

Trigger Timer Escalated to Decision required within
Handoff not accepted R4 breached Receiver's escalation contact 2 business h (Hygiene-Critical 1 h)
Resolution at risk 75% of X-target used Owner + CS (alert only) —
Resolution breached X-target passed Escalation contact by type 4 business h (Hygiene-Critical 2 h)
Silence breached R6 passed CS owner, then CS escalation (city queue) Same business day

E. Illustrative totals (used for consistency in Task 2)

Scenario Typical path Response Resolution Confirmation End to end (illustrative, not PadCare's actual performance)
S-01 missed collection, Hygiene-Critical Log → triage → Ops City Manager + SE visit task → evidence → confirm Ack ≤ 2 h; ETA ≤ 4 h Visit ≤ 24 h ≤ 5 business days ~1 day to fix; closed within ~1 week at most
S-02 billing, Service-Impacting Log → triage → Finance → CS → confirm Ack same day; ETA ≤ 1 business day ≤ 5 business days ≤ 5 business days ~5 business days to fix; ≤ ~2 weeks to closure

Response vs resolution — why they are separate

  • Response targets (R1–R6) are about the customer knowing where things stand. They are the same for every case type and owned mainly by CS.
  • Resolution targets (X1–X4) are about the problem being fixed. They vary by type and severity and are owned by whoever holds the case.

A case can meet every response target and still miss resolution, and vice versa. Measuring both separately shows which team is the bottleneck.

To validate with PadCare

  1. Is a 24 h corrective visit achievable in every city? (SE capacity, route planning)
  2. Finance's invoice correction cycle: is 5 business days realistic? Is there a monthly billing cut-off that should set the target?
  3. Working days and hours for CS and field teams (Sundays? holidays?).
  4. Service frequency by site type, to calibrate the 3-day missed-collection escalator.

Phase 3 — Challenges Map

Step references (e.g., 2.5, R6) point to 02_phase2/end_to_end_flow.md and sla_matrix.md. Coverage: ● fully addressed in v1 · ◐ partly (limitation stated).

A. Challenges Map (document version — goes at the top of the submission)

# Challenge (brief) Design choice that addresses it Where in the design Coverage
1 Complaints lost between channels Whoever receives an issue logs it, from any of the 6 channels, in a 2-minute Log step. The case is owned by the account's CS owner from the moment it is logged, or by the city CS queue if that person is on leave. A status enquiry about an issue with no case exposes the loss (flag Not logged at receipt) 1.1, 1.2, 2.2 · R1 ◐
2 Repeat vs new unknown Related-record panel shown before classification (open cases + same site/category in 90 days). The 3rd case in 90 days is marked "Recurrence", raises severity one level, and needs a root-cause note to resolve 2.1, 2.4, 2.5, 4.1 ●
3 Requests, status checks, account concerns all called "complaints" 4 case types with their own owner, path and closure evidence, chosen by 5 ordered questions. A status check is not a case; it is attached to its parent. Mixed messages are split into linked cases (S-03) 2.2, 2.3 · Phase 1 matrix ●
4 No clear handoff between teams Formal handoff: reason + required-info checklist + due time. The sender stays accountable until the receiver accepts or returns it; non-acceptance escalates. Work by another team that doesn't need ownership to move is a linked task with an owner and due date. CS remains the communication owner throughout 3.1–3.4, 4.3 · R4 ●
5 "Resolved" ≠ resolved Resolution evidence required by type (visit proof, invoice/credit note no., install record, action plan) before Awaiting Confirmation. Closure needs the customer's confirmation or a defined no-response rule. Rejection reopens the case; a recurrence within 14 days reopens it 4.1, 5.1–5.4 · V1–V3 ●
6 Can't see patterns Structured fields (city, site, customer, type, sub-category, severity, channel) and an event log for every status, owner and customer update. This enables, e.g., "% of missed-service complaints by city last quarter" ST6 · Phase 7 metrics ●
7 Customer has no visibility CS sends updates at fixed points (acknowledgement with case ref, ETA, any ETA change, resolution) plus a "maximum silence" timer per severity. Status enquiries are counted per case, so chasing is measured 2.6, 5.1 · R3, R5, R6 ◐
8 Severity by who shouts loudest Severity proposed by the system from impact answers (hygiene exposure now? sites affected? commitment broken?) plus automatic escalators for operational complaints (recurrence, 3+ sites, overdue days). Seniority, tone and revenue are not inputs. Overrides need a reason; Expedite use is reported 2.5 ●
