03_phase3/task1_reasoning.md

Phase 3 — Task 1 Narrative and Reasoning

The narrative below is the Task 1 "short narrative explaining key decisions — especially around classification, routing and SLAs". Each card is ≤ 6 lines. Candidate action: rewrite the final Reasoning note (§C) in your own words before submission. It is the part most likely to be quoted back to you in the walkthrough.

A. Key decisions (narrative)

Classification

1. Four case types; a status check is attached to an existing case, not created as a new one. (C-3, S-04) Each type needs a different owner, path and definition of "done". A missed collection ends with a visit, a billing issue with an invoice, a request with fulfilment, and an account concern with a plan. A status check has no work of its own. Making it a case would inflate complaint counts and create something that could be "closed" while the real issue stays open. Rejected: one "complaint" record with a free-text type, which is today's problem with a dropdown added. Trade-off: "Case" is a new word for teams.

2. Classification is five ordered questions, not a flat dropdown. (S-02, S-03, S-04, S-05) The samples are traps if read by keyword: S-04 mentions a missed service, S-05 mentions service quality, S-02 mentions a site move, and S-03 mentions overflow. Asking "already raised?" → "account-level?" → "billing?" → "failure?" → "new request?" in that order puts each one in the right type. Trade-off: a few seconds slower than picking from a list.

3. Split independent needs into linked cases; keep dependent needs inside one case. (S-03) The overflow needs relief this week; the extra unit may take weeks and approval. As one case, either the overflow waits for the installation, or the case closes before the unit arrives. Trade-off: judging "independent" needs training examples.

Severity and priority

4. Severity comes from impact rules, with three named levels and three escalators. The reporter's identity is never an input. (C-8) The levels test what is happening at the site (hygiene exposure now? service or billing commitment broken?), not who is asking. For operational complaints, recurrence, multi-site scope and overdue days raise the level automatically (billing escalates instead), so a polite report of the third odour complaint at a large account outranks a loud cosmetic one. Rejected: P1–P4 tiers set by judgement, which is how "loudest wins" happens today. Validate: the thresholds.

5. Priority is a computed queue order, not a second label. (C-8) Severity → time left before the deadline → flags (rejected, chased, recurrence) → age. An "Expedite" flag exists because influence is real, but it needs a reason and its use is reported. That makes escalation by influence visible instead of invisible.

Routing and ownership

6. Two owner fields: a resolution owner that moves, and a communication owner (CS) that stays. (C-4, C-7) Finance should investigate a billing complaint without becoming the customer's contact. The customer should hear from one person throughout. Trade-off: each side may assume the other updated the customer, so the rule is explicit: CS always sends updates.

7. Ownership moves on acceptance, not assignment. (C-4) Today a forwarded email counts as a handoff, and the issue sits in nobody's inbox. Here the sender stays accountable until the receiver accepts, or returns it saying what is missing. No answer escalates. Alternative: auto-reassign on breach. Rejected, because it moves the problem rather than forcing a decision.

8. The receiver logs it, and the case is owned from the moment it is created. (C-1) The account's CS owner owns every new case, or the city CS queue covers when that person is on leave. Logging takes about 2 minutes (D-15), because a form slower than a WhatsApp reply would not get used. Limitation: v1 still depends on people logging. Lost issues surface, and are counted, when customers chase.

Resolution, closure, SLAs

9. "Resolved" requires evidence per type; "Closed" requires the customer. (C-5) The system will not move a case to Awaiting Confirmation without the type's evidence (visit proof, credit note number, install record, action plan). CS then asks the customer. No reply after two reminders closes it as "No Response", which is reported separately from confirmed closures. A return within 14 days reopens it. Trade-off: some unresolved issues close silently, which is why the two closure types are reported separately.

10. SLAs separate response from resolution, start when the customer told us, and pause only for the customer. (C-1, C-4, C-7)

  • Response targets (acknowledge, ETA, maximum silence) are the same for every type. They solve visibility without a portal.
  • Resolution targets vary by type and severity. A Hygiene-Critical visit must happen within 24 calendar hours, because waste builds up at weekends too; billing gets 5 business days, so the correction lands before the next invoice.
  • Starting from "received" makes late logging visible. Allowing only customer pauses means internal waits can't be hidden.

All targets are proposals to calibrate with real data. The 24 h visit depends on SE capacity per city (A-20).

B. Decision rationale table (for interview preparation)

Decision Problem solved Why preferred Alternative considered Trade-off Validate with PadCare
4 case types + status attached to parent C-3, C-5 Different owners and evidence per type Single complaint record; 5 types incl. status New vocabulary Do CS teams recognise the 4 types?
Ordered classification questions C-3 Resolves keyword traps in S-02/03/04/05 Flat dropdown Slightly slower Reclassification rate after launch
Split independent needs C-3, C-5 Separate closure conditions Single case Admin + judgement Training examples
Impact severity + escalators C-8, C-2 Rules, not voices Judgement-based tiers Coarse; thresholds unproven 3-day / 3-site / 3rd-in-90-days thresholds
Computed priority + reported Expedite C-8 Transparent queue Manual priority Less manual control Who may expedite
Resolution owner + communication owner C-4, C-7 One voice to the customer Single owner Coordination rule needed CS capacity
Ownership on acceptance C-4 No ownerless gap Transfer on assignment; auto-reassign Sender burden Field acceptance practicality (SEs)
Receiver logs; owner from creation C-1 Removes single-person dependency Central intake team Logging discipline CS rota for the shared inbox
Evidence + customer-confirmed closure C-5 "Done" is verifiable Close on reply Silent no-response closures Customer willingness to confirm
Response/resolution split; received-at clocks C-1, C-4, C-7 Shows which team is the bottleneck Single "resolution time" More targets to manage 24 h visit feasibility; Finance cycle

C. Task 1 Reasoning note (draft — about 6 lines on A4; rewrite in your own words)

The flow answers what PadCare can't today: did we get it, who owns it, is it fixed, has it happened before. The receiver logs it, and a CS owner holds it from creation (C1). Ordered classification keeps status checks, requests and account concerns out of the complaint queue (C3). A history panel and a recurrence rule surface repeats (C2, C6). Ownership moves only on acceptance (C4), closure needs evidence plus the customer's confirmation (C5), and severity follows hygiene impact and recurrence, not the reporter's seniority (C8). The weakest areas are C1 and C7: v1 still depends on people logging and updating.

Word count: ~95 (≈ 6 lines at A4 width, 11 pt).

04_phase4/task2_walkthroughs.md

Phase 4 — Task 2: Two Complaints Walked Through the Design

  • Selection: S-01 (missed collection, operational) and S-02 (billing, satisfies the "#2 or #5" rule) [D-07].
  • Step references (1.2, 2.5, R4…) are to 02_phase2/end_to_end_flow.md and sla_matrix.md.
  • Times are illustrative, chosen to be realistic within the proposed SLAs. They are not PadCare performance data. Business hours: 09:00–18:00 Mon–Sat [A-12].
  • ⚠ F-x marks where the walkthrough exposed a problem. Findings and fixes are in design_review.md.

Walkthrough A — S-01: "Collection was not collected this month. Please plan the visit ASAP, as it's a hygiene issue."

Setting (illustrative): a corporate office site; monthly collection; the Client SPOC (facility manager) WhatsApps their CS contact.

Intake captured at 1.2 (by the CS person who received the WhatsApp)

  • Customer, site: looked up from master data.
  • Reporter: SPOC — name, phone, role "Facility manager".
  • Channel: WhatsApp to CS.
  • Received at: Day 1 (Mon) 10:05, taken from the message timestamp.
  • Customer's words: verbatim, with a screenshot.
  • Logger's best guess: Operational complaint.

Timeline

Time Step Accountable owner Status What happens SLA check
D1 10:05 1.1 — — WhatsApp received by the CS owner Clocks start (received at)
D1 10:40 1.2–1.3 CS (account owner) New Logged in about 2 min; customer and site valid R1 (1 h for Hygiene-Critical, HC): 35 min ✓
D1 10:45 2.1 CS New Related-record panel: no open cases. One earlier missed collection at this site 50 days ago (repeat count 2: suggested Recurrence of link; the Recurrence flag starts at the 3rd). Schedule shows this month's visit (due on the 6th) as Rescheduled with no new date [A-02] —
D1 10:50 2.2–2.3 CS New Q1 no (new issue) → Q2 no → Q3 no → Q4 yes: PadCare missed a committed service → Operational complaint / Missed collection. No duplicate. "Plan the visit" is the fix itself, not a second need → no split —
D1 11:05 2.5 CS New Impact questions. Hygiene exposure now? CS asks the SPOC: bins full on two floors → yes. Overdue? 7 days past schedule (escalator ≥ 3 days). Severity = Hygiene-Critical. The customer's word "hygiene" triggered the question, but the answer came from facts (C-8) R2 (1 h from log): 25 min ✓
D1 11:15 2.6 CS New Acknowledgement on WhatsApp: case ref, "missed collection, marked urgent; visit time by 2 pm"; logged as a customer update R3 (2 h): 1 h 10 ✓
D1 11:20 3.1–3.2 CS (until acceptance) Assigned → SE-1 Routed to SE-1, the site's scheduled SE. Checklist: site, floors, access contact, severity, problem R4 deadline 12:20
D1 12:20 4.3 CS Assigned SE-1 has not accepted: on route, phone not checked. Auto-escalation to the Ops City Manager ⚠ F-4 R4 breached → decision due in 1 h
D1 12:45 4.3 CS Assigned → SE-2 Ops City Manager records the decision: reassign to SE-2 (nearby route) Decision in 25 min ✓
D1 12:55 3.2 SE-2 In Progress SE-2 accepts on mobile [A-05]; ownership transfers —
D1 13:05 R5 SE-2 (CS communicates) In Progress CS sends the ETA: "visit today 16:30" R5 (4 h): 3 h ✓
D1 16:30–16:50 4.1 SE-2 In Progress Collection done on all floors; photo; SPOC signs off in the SE app [A-21] —
D1 16:55 4.4 SE-2 → CS Awaiting Confirmation Evidence recorded: visit record + photo + sign-off. Ownership returns to CS. ⚠ F-6: nothing checks that next month's visit is back on the schedule X1 (24 h): 6 h 50 ✓
D1 17:30 5.1 CS Awaiting Confirmation CS sends the photo and asks "Is this resolved?" ⚠ F-5: the SPOC already signed off on site; asking again is duplicate effort V1 (same day for HC) ✓
D2 09:40 5.2–5.3 CS Closed – Confirmed SPOC: "Yes, thanks." CS closes with reason Confirmed Within V2 ✓

Classification rationale (why)

  • Operational, not a service request: the customer asks PadCare to make good a missed commitment, not to add anything.
  • Hygiene-Critical because the bins were full (exposure now) and the visit was 7 days overdue. It would be the same severity if a junior employee had reported it politely.
  • Priority: top of the city queue (HC + R4 breach flag).

Ownership trail

CS (New) → CS accountable while assigned to SE-1 → Ops City Manager decides → SE-2 (In Progress) → CS (Awaiting Confirmation) → Closed. CS was the communication owner throughout.

Duration

  • Fix: 6 h 50 (target 24 h).
  • Closure: about 23.5 h.
  • The SE escalation cost about 1.5 h of the fix time.

Alternative paths tested

If… Then…
The schedule shows the visit as Completed but the customer says it was not Data-integrity flag (4.1): cannot be resolved without an Ops City Manager note; a possible SE-conduct case is created and linked
Bins are not full and the visit is only 1 day overdue Service-Impacting; X1 = 3 business days; added to the next route
This was the 3rd missed collection in 90 days Recurrence → severity already at maximum; Ops City Manager root-cause review; KAM informed if it is a KAM account
SPOC replies "only 2 of 4 floors collected" Rejected → In Progress with SE-2; rejection count 1; the SLA continues from the original receipt

Walkthrough B — S-02: "Your invoice for September shows charges for the Hyderabad site, but we shifted to a new location in July. Please correct the address."

Setting (illustrative): a multi-site corporate customer; the SPOC emails the generic support inbox.

Intake captured at 1.2 (by the CS person on inbox duty — not the account's CS owner)

  • Customer: looked up.
  • Site: Hyderabad site (the old record).
  • Reporter: SPOC — email, role "Admin / facilities".
  • Channel: support email.
  • Received at: D1 (Wed) 11:30.
  • Customer's words: email text pasted.
  • Logger's best guess: Billing.

Timeline

Time Step Accountable owner Status What happens SLA check
D1 11:30 1.1 — — Email arrives in the support inbox Clocks start
D1 13:00 1.2–1.3 Account CS owner (auto) New The inbox-duty CS logs it. Site exists, but the customer says it moved → "Unverified site" warning (not blocking). The case lands with the account's CS owner, not the inbox person (C-1) R1 (2 business h): 1 h 30 ✓
D1 14:30 2.1 CS New Panel: no open cases; no billing cases in 90 days. Schedule: services Jul–Sep recorded against the Hyderabad site record —
D1 14:40 2.2 CS New Triage question from Phase 1: address only, or charges for a vacated site? CS calls the SPOC: services continue at the new location, the amount is right, but their accounts team cannot process an invoice with the old address. Q1 no → Q2 no → Q3 yes → Billing complaint / Wrong site-address —
D1 14:50 2.5 CS New Impact: no hygiene exposure; invoice is wrong. ⚠ F-1: the Low-Impact definition ("document error with no effect on amount") and the Service-Impacting definition ("billed incorrectly") both fit. CS chooses Service-Impacting because the invoice is unusable R2 (4 business h from log) ✓
D1 15:00 2.6 CS New Acknowledgement email: case ref; Finance will correct; next update by tomorrow R3 (same day) ✓
D1 15:10 3.2 CS (until acceptance) Assigned → Finance Handoff checklist: invoice no. (Sept), disputed item = billing address, expectation = reissued invoice, customer email attached R4 (4 business h)
D1 16:30 3.2 CS Assigned Finance returns it: "new address and effective date missing" ⚠ F-7. As designed, the case is back with CS in Assigned. CS cannot put it On Hold from Assigned — the state diagram only allows On Hold from In Progress ⚠ F-2. Workaround: CS moves it to In Progress, then On Hold —
D1 16:45 4.2 CS On Hold – Customer CS emails the SPOC for the new address and move date. Clock paused —
D2 10:15 4.2 CS In Progress Customer replies: new address, effective 15 July. Clock resumes (paused 2 h 30 business time) —
D2 10:30 3.2 CS Assigned → Finance Re-handoff with complete information R4 deadline 14:30
D2 11:30 3.2 Finance In Progress Finance accepts R4: 1 h ✓
D2 12:00 R5 Finance (CS communicates) In Progress CS update: "corrected invoice by Monday" R5 (1 business day + hold) ✓
D2 15:00 4.1 Finance In Progress Finance finds that the July and August invoices also carry the old address; the customer only mentioned September ⚠ F-8. Root cause: the site master record was never updated [D-18] —
D2 15:15 4.4 Finance In Progress Finance needs the site record corrected by its owner (assumed the Hyderabad Ops City Manager [A-18]). The only tool is a handoff, which would move ownership away from Finance. Finance emails the Ops City Manager instead — today's informal behaviour ⚠ F-3 —
D3 (Fri) 15:00 — Finance In Progress Site record updated: new address, effective 15 July —
D5 (Mon) 12:00 4.4 Finance → CS Awaiting Confirmation Reissued Jul/Aug/Sep invoices (numbers recorded) + master-data change reference = evidence X2 (5 business days): ~3.8 business days net of hold ✓
D5 14:00 5.1 CS Awaiting Confirmation CS emails the reissued invoices; asks the customer to confirm V1 ✓
D7 (Wed) 10:00 5.2 CS Awaiting Confirmation Automatic reminder 1 (day 2) —
D7 15:20 5.3 CS Closed – Confirmed Customer: "Received, all fine." Closed Within V2 ✓

Classification rationale (why)

  • Billing, not a service request to change site details: the customer's need is a corrected invoice.
    • The site-record fix is PadCare's internal root cause. It is not a separate customer request.
  • Service-Impacting: the customer cannot use the invoice. The rule wording had to be stretched to reach this (F-1).
  • No severity escalator applied. The fact that three invoices were affected only surfaced during investigation.

Ownership trail

CS (New) → CS accountable while assigned to Finance → returned to CS → CS (On Hold – Customer) → CS → Finance (In Progress, with an untracked request to the Ops City Manager) → CS (Awaiting Confirmation) → Closed.

Duration

  • Resolution: about 3.8 business days net of the 2.5 h customer hold (target 5).
  • Closure: 6 business days.
  • The missing-information return cost most of a day.

Alternative paths tested

If… Then…
The customer was charged for services at the vacated site Sub-category → Charged for service not delivered; Finance issues a credit note; Ops must explain why visits were recorded at an address the customer had left (data-integrity flag, linked operational case)
Finance finds the invoice correct (e.g., the move was never notified) Evidence = documented explanation; CS communicates it; if the customer rejects twice → escalate (KAM if the account has one)
The customer never confirms Reminders at day 2 and 4 → Closed – No Response at day 5; reported separately
The October invoice is wrong again Recurrence (new billing case linked). With the master fixed, this should not happen; v2 automatic check (F-9)

Task 2 Reasoning note (draft — rewrite in your own words)

Both cases met every proposed SLA, but walking them exposed gaps the flow diagram hides. The billing case had no clean way for Finance to get the site record fixed without giving up ownership. So I added linked tasks: work by another team that does not move accountability. Finance's return for missing information showed the intake form must ask for the new address and effective date when the sub-category is a wrong site. It also showed my state diagram blocked "On Hold" after a return. In the missed collection, a field SE could not realistically accept within an hour, so Hygiene-Critical visits now route to the Ops City Manager to dispatch. I also caught myself rating an address-only invoice error under two different severity definitions, and tightened the billing definition.

Word count: ~120 (≈ 6–7 lines at A4 width). Trim further if needed.

04_phase4/design_review.md

Phase 4 — Design Review (findings from the walkthroughs)

Each finding states: what broke, why it matters, the fix, and whether it is applied now (v1 — the Task 1 design is updated) or deferred (v2).

ID Found in Type What broke Why it matters Fix Version
F-1 S-02, step 2.5 Inconsistency Phase 1 rated S-02 Service-Impacting; Phase 2 defines Low-Impact as "a document error with no effect on the amount", which describes S-02 exactly. Two defined rules give two answers Severity must be the same whoever triages (C-8); a rule that depends on interpretation brings back judgement calls Billing severity is redefined by whether the customer can act on the invoice: Service-Impacting = amount wrong or the invoice cannot be processed by the customer (wrong entity, site or address). Low-Impact = a cosmetic error that does not stop processing. The "unusable invoice" test is asked as an impact question v1
F-2 S-02, step 3.3 State-machine gap A returned handoff left the case in Assigned with the sender, but On Hold – Customer is only reachable from In Progress. CS needed a workaround A spec a developer builds literally would block a real path; workarounds corrupt timestamps Return → In Progress with the sender (the sender was already the accountable owner). Transition updated v1
F-3 S-02, step 4.4 Missing concept Finance needed another team (the site master-data owner) to do a piece of work. The only tool was a handoff, which would move ownership; Finance fell back to email This recreates C-04's "forwarded emails" inside the new system Add linked tasks: owner, due date, done/not done, inside a case. The case owner stays accountable; the task owner is accountable for the task; overdue tasks escalate like handoffs; mandatory tasks block resolution. Also used for SE visits (F-4) and S-03-style installations v1
F-4 S-01, step 3.2 Practicality Hygiene-Critical cases were assigned to an SE in the field with a 1 h acceptance target. The SE was on route and did not respond; escalation worked but cost ~1.5 h The most urgent cases depend on the person least able to respond to notifications For Hygiene-Critical operational complaints, the resolution owner = Ops City Manager (desk-based, accepts within 1 h). The SE visit is a linked task (F-3). Service-Impacting / Low-Impact still go to the scheduled SE (4 business h acceptance is workable). Trade-off: more load on Ops City Managers; validate volume v1
F-5 S-01, step 5.1 Duplicate effort The SPOC signed off on site in the SE app, then CS asked "is this resolved?" again Asking twice irritates customers and delays closure If the sign-off is by the reporter or the SPOC, it counts as confirmation → Closed – Confirmed on site; CS sends a closure note instead of a question. A sign-off by anyone else (e.g., security) still triggers the CS request v1
F-6 S-01, step 4.4 Root cause left open One make-up visit resolved the case, but the regular schedule had dropped (Rescheduled with no date). Next month could be missed again The case closes "resolved" while the cause continues; it returns as a recurrence (C-02, C-05) Evidence for Missed collection adds: "next scheduled visit confirmed in the schedule" (date) v1
F-7 S-02, step 3.3 Intake gap Finance returned the case for the missing new address and effective date Each return costs about a day; the information was predictable from the sub-category Task 3: when sub-category = Wrong site/address, correct address + effective date are mandatory at triage (hard validation before a Finance handoff) v1 (Phase 5)
F-8 S-02, step 4.1 Scope blind spot The customer named September; July and August were also wrong Fixing only the reported invoice guarantees a second complaint Finance handoff checklist adds "identify all invoices affected since the effective date"; the evidence lists every reissued invoice v1
F-9 S-02, closure Verification gap Nothing confirms the next invoice is correct after the master-data fix The fix is assumed, not verified Automatically flag the account's next invoice for a check (needs billing data in PadCareOne [A-03]) v2
F-10 S-01, R3 Measurement risk If CS replies informally on WhatsApp ("checking") before logging, R3 is measured only from the logged acknowledgement Fair performance data; avoids gaming At Log, allow "customer already acknowledged at [time]" to be recorded as a customer update. Only acknowledgements that include a case reference count towards R3 v1 (minor)
F-12 Phase 6 test design (TC-04 B) Inconsistency The recurrence escalator would make a 3rd billing complaint Hygiene-Critical Meaningless severity; no X2 target exists for it Billing is capped at Service-Impacting; recurrence triggers escalation instead v1
F-11 Both Assumption exposed The site master-data owner is unknown [A-18]; F-3 tasks need a named owner A task with no owner is the C-04 problem again Name the owner during PadCare validation. Default until then: the Ops City Manager of the site's city Open question

What I would change but deliberately did not

Idea Why not in v1
Auto-confirm closure when the SE app sign-off exists for every case The sign-off can come from someone who did not report the issue; the confirmation must come from the person who complained or the SPOC
Merge Finance and CS into one "billing desk" owner Changes PadCare's organisation, which is beyond a product design
Severity escalator for "3+ invoices affected" Known only after investigation; severity is set at triage. Use the recurrence rule instead if it repeats

Changes applied to the Task 1 design (v1)

Changes applied in 02_phase2/end_to_end_flow.md, marked † in the final document:

  1. Billing severity definitions (F-1).
  2. Return → In Progress with the sender (F-2), in the state diagram and status table.
  3. Linked tasks concept (F-3) in ST3/ST4.
  4. Hygiene-Critical operational routing to the Ops City Manager plus an SE task (F-4).
  5. On-site sign-off as confirmation (F-5).
  6. Missed-collection evidence includes the next scheduled visit (F-6).
  7. Finance checklist: all affected invoices (F-8).
  8. Prior-acknowledgement capture (F-10).

F-7 goes into the Task 3 spec (Phase 5). F-9 is listed as v2.

05_phase5/intake_form_spec.md

Phase 5 — Task 3: Intake and Classification Form — Functional Specification

Scope: stages ST1 (Intake) and ST2 (Triage) of 02_phase2/end_to_end_flow.md v1.1. Validation rule IDs (VR-xx) are defined in validation_rules.md; exception flows in exception_handling.md.

1. Form structure

One form in PadCareOne, filled in two steps by possibly different people [D-15]:

Step Who Goal Saves to status
Log Whoever received the issue (CS, KAM, SE on mobile [A-05]) Capture the issue in about 2 minutes; never lose it (C-1) New
Triage CS (account owner or city queue) Complete the data; classify, link, set severity and route (C-2, C-3, C-8) New → Assigned / In Progress

When a field is required (column Req.):

  • L — required to save the Log.
  • T — required to complete Triage.
  • H — required before the named handoff.
  • C — conditional (see Shown when).
  • O — optional.
  • S — system-set (read-only).

Status enquiries use a short path: Log → link to the parent case → record the update. No Triage and no new case (§4).

2. Fields table

2.1 Identity and source (all case types)

# Field Type · Source Req. Shown when Notes, validation, default
1 Case ID Text · system S Always Format PC-YYMM-NNNNN; unique; assigned on save
2 Logged at / Logged by Datetime, user · system S Always Server time; current user
3 Channel Dropdown · user L Always WhatsApp to CS · Support email · Phone call to CS · CS check-in call · KAM escalation · SE on site · Other (requires text). Default by logger role: SE → "SE on site", KAM → "KAM escalation"
4 Received at Datetime · user (default now) L Always When the customer told PadCare; starts all SLA clocks [D-25]. Not in the future; ≤ Logged at (VR-05). More than R1 before now → info "will count as late registration" (VR-06). More than 30 days → reason required
5 Customer already acknowledged at Datetime · user O Always F-10. Between Received at and now (VR-29). Stored as a customer update; counts towards R3 only if a case reference was given
6 Source reference Text · user O Channel = email / WhatsApp Email subject or message ID; WhatsApp sender number
7 Attachments Upload · user O Always Screenshot, email file, photo. JPG, PNG, PDF, EML, MSG, DOCX, XLSX; ≤ 10 MB each; ≤ 5 files (VR-25)

# Field Type · Source Req. Shown when Notes, validation, default

Warning, not a block (VR-03). Must be resolved at Triage: pick the correct site or create a master-data task [A-18]

The first "Yes" sets field 17. Skipping ahead is allowed for experienced users; the questions are recorded

Billing: Wrong amount · Wrong site/address · Charged for service not delivered · Duplicate invoice · Credit note pending · Other. Service request: Additional unit · Remove/relocate unit · Change schedule · Extra/one-off visit · Site details change · Document/information request. 49 Priority Computed · system S Severity → SLA state → flags → age [D-20]
50 Expedite Checkbox + reason · KAM / Ops City Manager only O Reason required; reported (VR-28)
51 Next owner User/queue · system-suggested by routing table T Hygiene-Critical operational → Ops City Manager (F-4); billing → Finance; etc. Handoff checklist by type (VR-31)
52 Acknowledgement sent Datetime + text · user T Must include the case ref; logged as a customer update (R3)

3. Conditions and dependencies (summary)

3.1 Required fields by case type

Field group Operational Billing Service request Account-level Status enquiry
Identity, channel, received at, reporter, words L L L L L
Customer L L L L L
Site L L L O → Sites affected T L (prefills parent search)
Sub-category T T T T —
Location on site T — T — —
Scheduled visit T (Missed/Late) — — — —
Invoice no. / month / expected outcome / can process — T + H — — —
Correct address + effective date — H (Wrong site/address or "moved" flag) — — —
Requested-by + committed date, current problem? — — T — —
Hygiene exposure now? T — — T —
Severity T T hidden T inherits parent
Parent case — — — — L (or "No existing case")

3.2 Behaviour by channel

  • SE on site: opened from the SE mobile view; the site is pre-filled from the current visit; a photo is suggested. If the SE has no access, CS logs with channel "SE on site" and the SE's name (VR-30).
  • KAM escalation: reporter role is often "Customer leadership". The severity section shows the note "Reporter role does not affect severity" (C-8).
  • CS check-in call: after saving, "Add another issue from this call" keeps the reporter, channel and received at pre-filled (one call, several cases).
  • Email / WhatsApp: source reference shown; attachment prompt.

3.3 Dynamic behaviour

  • Changing the customer clears the site, links and type-specific lookups, and re-runs VR-02, VR-11 and VR-12.
  • Changing the case type keeps the shared fields and hides (does not delete) type-specific fields until Triage is saved.
  • The related cases panel refreshes on any change to customer, site or sub-category.

4. Status enquiry path (form behaviour)

  1. Type = Status enquiry → the form collapses to: customer, site (optional), reporter, channel, received at, words, Parent case (lookup: this customer's open cases plus those closed in the last 30 days, best matches first by site and sub-category).
  2. A parent is selected → save creates a follow-up on the parent, not a case:
    • followup_received event;
    • parent flag "customer chased";
    • the parent's communication owner gets a task "update customer" due within R3.
  3. If the parent is Awaiting Confirmation → prompt: "Ask whether it is resolved."
  4. If the parent is Closed → the reopen / recurrence rules apply (exception_handling.md E-1).
  5. "No existing case found" → the form converts to the full form for the underlying issue:
    • Not logged at receipt = Yes;
    • Customer-stated original report date is required and becomes Received at.

5. Task 3 Reasoning note (draft — rewrite in your own words)

The hardest decision was customer–site validation: block or warn? Blocking guarantees clean data for repeat detection and reporting (C-2, C-6). But it means an issue that doesn't fit the master data is never logged (C-1), and S-02 is that case: the customer moved and our records didn't. So a missing or disputed site is a warning at Log that must be resolved at Triage. A site belonging to a different customer stays a hard error, because that is a wrong pick, not missing data. I applied the same logic to an unmatched customer. The trade-off: some records sit briefly with unverified data, which is why Triage has a short SLA.

Phase 5 — Validation Rules

Severity of a rule:

  • E = hard error — blocks the save or the transition.
  • S = soft block — the user must explicitly choose an option to continue.
  • W = warning — informs; does not block.

Checked at: L = Log save · T = Triage completion · H = handoff · X = status transition. Origin: the sample complaint, challenge or finding that motivates the rule. Rules without a specific origin are standard data integrity.

Role × transition matrix (VR-27)

✓ = allowed · — = not allowed.

Transition CS (comm. owner) Current resolution owner (SE / Finance / Ops City Manager) KAM Ops City Manager (as escalation contact) System
Log (create New) ✓ ✓ (SE, KAM can log) ✓ ✓ —
Complete Triage, set severity ✓ — ✓ (account-level only) ✓ —
Hand off (→ Assigned) ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ —
Accept / return (Assigned →) Receiver only Receiver only Receiver only Receiver, or reassign as escalation contact —
→ On Hold – Customer / resume ✓ — ✓ (account-level) — Resume on time-out
→ Awaiting Confirmation (with evidence) ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ —
→ Closed – Confirmed ✓ — ✓ (account-level: Plan Agreed) — ✓ only from a valid on-site sign-off (F-5)
→ Closed – No Response — — — — ✓ (V2/V4 timers only)
→ Closed – Cancelled (duplicate / invalid) ✓ with reason — ✓ with reason ✓ with reason —
Reopen ✓ — ✓ ✓ —
Change final severity after Triage ✓ with reason — — ✓ with reason —

Nobody can move a case directly to Closed – Confirmed without resolution evidence (VR-33), including administrators. Corrections to closed cases are made by reopening.

Error vs warning: the principle used

  • Hard errors protect things that cannot be fixed later without harm:

    • a wrong customer–site link (repeat detection breaks);
    • missing invoice data at the Finance handoff (causes a return);
    • closure without evidence (C-5).

  • Warnings and soft blocks cover things a person must judge:

    • a possible duplicate;
    • a recurrence;
    • a move date that suggests the invoice may be correct.

    A warning never stops an issue from being logged (C-1).

05_phase5/exception_handling.md

Phase 5 — Exception Handling

The first three are the exceptions the brief names explicitly for Task 3. The rest are those the master prompt and walkthroughs require. Each is written as short points, as the brief asks.

E-1. Status check (S-04)

  • Logger selects Status enquiry (Q1 = Yes) → the form collapses; Parent case is required (VR-09).
  • Parent open → follow-up added; "customer chased" flag raises priority. The communication owner gets an "update customer" task due within R3. No new case.
  • Parent Awaiting Confirmation → CS asks whether it is resolved; the answer is recorded as the confirmation outcome.
  • Parent closed ≤ 14 days ago and the customer says it is not fixed → reopen the parent (reason required).
  • Parent closed > 14 days ago → a new case linked Recurrence of.
  • No parent found → convert to the full form: Not logged at receipt = Yes; Received at = the customer-stated original date (VR-06 reason). Counted as a lost complaint (C-1).
  • Parent belongs to another customer → blocked (VR-10).
  • An answered status enquiry never changes the parent's status (C-5).

E-2. Repeat complaint (C-2)

  • Same incident, still open (VR-11 → "Same — add as follow-up"): becomes a follow-up, as in E-1.
  • Same incident, second reporter (e.g., End User emails while the SPOC WhatsApps): "Same — duplicate report" → saved as Closed – Cancelled – Duplicate, linked to the parent; the second reporter is added as a parent contact. One case, two people informed.
  • New incident of the same kind after an earlier one was resolved: a new case. The system suggests Recurrence of when the earlier case is within 90 days.
    • At the 3rd case → Recurrence flag, severity +1 level, Ops City Manager root-cause review, KAM informed (VR-12).
  • Same site, different sub-category: shown in the panel as context only; no forced link.
  • The system never merges automatically. Every link records who decided and when [D-14].

E-3. Request raised for the wrong site or customer

  • Site belongs to a different customer → hard error at Log (VR-02); pick the correct pair.
  • Site not in master / customer says it moved (S-02) → Log continues with the "Unverified site" flag and Site as stated. Triage must:
    • choose the correct existing site, or
    • create a site-record correction task for the master-data owner [A-18], which blocks resolution if mandatory (F-3).
  • Customer not in master → logged against "Unmatched customer" with the stated name; Triage cannot complete until matched (VR-01). Unmatched cases appear on the city CS queue.
  • Wrong customer or site discovered after Triage:
    • CS changes it with a reason (event logged);
    • SLA clocks are unchanged (same issue, same received time);
    • related-record checks re-run;
    • existing links to the old customer's cases are flagged for review.
  • Reporter not from the customer on record (e.g., a building management company): logged against the actual customer, with reporter role "Other".

E-4. Multiple issues in one message (S-03, check-in calls)

  • Split check (field 21) after classification: independent needs → "Create linked case" with shared fields pre-filled, link type Split from.
  • Dependent needs stay as actions in one case (e.g., "missed and charged" → operational complaint + credit-note task if the miss is confirmed).
  • A service request reporting a current problem → soft block VR-22 (create the linked complaint or give a reason).
  • Check-in calls: "Add another issue from this call" keeps the reporter, channel and received time.

E-5. Missing mandatory information

  • At Log: only the identity, customer, reporter and words fields block saving. Everything else can wait for Triage.
  • At Triage: type-specific requirements (§3.1 of the spec) block completion. The case stays New, and Triage SLA R2 keeps running, so a stalled triage is visible.
  • At handoff: checklist VR-31 blocks the handoff. Finance can also return a case with a reason, which goes back to In Progress with the sender (F-2).
  • Information only the customer has: On Hold – Customer (clock paused; reminders at day 2 and 4; closes at day 7 with a final message).

E-6. Invalid attachments

  • Wrong type, oversize, more than 5 files, or an unreadable file → that file is rejected with the reason (VR-25). The rest of the form still saves; the user is not forced to re-enter anything.
  • A WhatsApp screenshot that is too large → prompt to compress, or attach a PDF.

E-7. Unauthorised status changes

  • Blocked by the role × transition matrix (VR-27), with the message naming the role and transition.
  • Attempts are logged (an audit event), not just refused.
  • Closure without evidence is impossible for every role (VR-33); a closed case is corrected only by reopening it.

E-8. Customer non-response

  • At Awaiting Confirmation: reminders at business days 2 and 4 → Closed – No Response at day 5 (V2).
    • Excluded from the confirmed-closure rate.
    • If the reporter or SPOC signed off on site, the case is already confirmed (F-5).
  • At On Hold – Customer: reminders at days 2 and 4 → closed at day 7, closure reason No Response (sub-reason: information request) (V4).
  • Hygiene-Critical cases closing as No Response trigger an SE check on the next scheduled visit (record a task).

E-9. Reopening after closure

  • Within 14 days, same issue → reopen (CS/KAM/Ops City Manager, with a reason):
    • goes to In Progress with the last resolution owner;
    • reopen count +1;
    • the resolution clock restarts from the reopen time.
  • After 14 days → a new case linked Recurrence of; feeds VR-12.
  • Duplicate or invalid found to be valid → reopen with a reason (any CS).

E-10. Cancelled or invalid records

  • Closure reasons: Cancelled – Duplicate (link required), or Cancelled – Invalid with a sub-reason:
    • not a PadCare issue (e.g., the customer's own cleaning staff);
    • logged in error;
    • test record.
  • Who can cancel: CS, KAM, or the Ops City Manager. Cancelled records stay in the register and in the volume-by-channel counts, but are excluded from the complaint metrics.

  • 7 are out of scope by design (VR-18, 19, 20, 22, 23, 24, 30). They are specific to S-01, S-03, S-05 or SE logging, and the brief asks for tests on one complaint.
  • 10 billing-relevant gaps (VR-01, 04, 10, 14, 16, 21, 26, 28, 29, 34) would be added in a full test plan.

None of the gaps affects the six document test cases.

C. Finding raised by test design

ID Found while writing Problem Fix (v1)
F-12 TC-04 variant B The recurrence escalator raises severity one level, capped at Hygiene-Critical. A 3rd billing complaint would therefore become Hygiene-Critical, which is meaningless for billing and has no X2 target Severity escalators cap at Service-Impacting for billing. A billing recurrence instead triggers escalation (Finance escalation contact + KAM informed). Applied in end_to_end_flow.md §2.5 † and the VR-12 text
07_phase7/data_model.md

Phase 7 — Data Model (minimum to support the workflow)

Principle: reuse PadCareOne's existing records [A-01] [A-02]. Add five module tables. History lives in one append-only event log, not separate history tables [D-39].

1. Entities

Entity New / existing Purpose Key fields
Customer Existing [A-01] Account customer_id, name, status, cs_owner_id, kam_id (nullable), primary_city
Site Existing [A-01] Service location site_id, customer_id, city, address, status
Contact Existing / created at Log Reporter / SPOC contact_id, customer_id, name, phone, email, role
User Existing PadCare staff user_id, role (CS, SE, OPS_CM, KAM, FIN), city, available (leave flag)
ScheduledVisit Existing [A-02] Service schedule visit_id, site_id, scheduled_date, status (Scheduled / Completed / Rescheduled / Missed)
Case New The register see §2
CaseLink New Relationships between cases link_id, from_case_id, to_case_id, link_type (Duplicate of · Recurrence of · Split from · Child of · Related), created_by, created_at
CaseEvent New (append-only) Status, owner, handoff, customer update, follow-up, severity, escalation, confirmation history; SLA clocks event_id, case_id, event_type, actor_id, actor_role, occurred_at, from_value, to_value, reason, payload (JSON: e.g., the update text, the follow-up's contact, the handoff checklist)
CaseTask New Linked tasks (F-3) task_id, case_id, task_type (SE visit · Site-record correction · Commercial approval · Installation · Other), owner_id, due_at, mandatory (bool), status (Open / Done / Cancelled), done_at, evidence_ref
Attachment New Files attachment_id, case_id, task_id (nullable), purpose (Customer evidence · Resolution evidence · Other), file_type, size, uploaded_by, uploaded_at
SlaPolicy New (config) Targets from sla_matrix.md target_id (R1…V4), case_type, severity, duration, calendar (calendar / business)

The master prompt's other entities map as follows:

  • Assignment history, status history, SLA event, customer communication → CaseEvent types.
  • Resolution record, customer confirmation → Case fields (current state) + CaseEvent (history).

2. Case — fields (mirrors intake_form_spec.md)

Group Fields
Identity case_id (PK, PC-YYMM-NNNNN), logged_at, logged_by
Source channel, received_at, prior_ack_at, source_ref
Customer customer_id (or unmatched_customer_name), site_id (nullable for account-level), site_unverified (bool), site_as_stated, city (derived)
Reporter reporter_contact_id, copy_spoc (bool)
Classification case_type, sub_category, classification_answers (Q1–Q5), not_logged_at_receipt (bool)
Type-specific location_on_site, scheduled_visit_id, invoice_no, invoice_month, disputed_amount, expected_outcome, customer_can_process (bool), correct_address, effective_date, quantity, requested_by_date, committed_date, current_problem_reported (bool), commercial_approval_needed (bool), sites_affected (array), customer_asks_for
Severity / priority hygiene_exposure_now, sites_affected_count, recurrence_count, system_severity, final_severity, override_reason, expedite (bool), expedite_reason
Ownership resolution_owner_id, pending_owner_id (during Assigned), communication_owner_id, escalation_level
Lifecycle status, triaged_at, resolved_at, closed_at, closure_reason (Confirmed · Confirmed on site · Plan Agreed · No Response · Cancelled – Duplicate · Cancelled – Invalid), closure_sub_reason, reopen_count, rejection_count, followup_count, customer_chased (bool)
Resolution evidence_type, evidence_refs (invoice/credit-note numbers, visit_id), root_cause_note, next_visit_confirmed_date
Confirmation confirmation_outcome (Confirmed · Confirmed on site · Rejected · No response), confirmed_by_contact_id, confirmed_at

3. Relationships

4. Constraints (enforced in the database or service layer)

# Constraint Supports
K1 case.site.customer_id = case.customer_id VR-02, C-2
K2 If status ≠ Closed → resolution_owner_id NOT NULL and communication_owner_id NOT NULL C-4: never ownerless
K3 status = Assigned ⇔ pending_owner_id NOT NULL 3.2 handoff
K4 status = Closed → closure_reason NOT NULL; closure_reason ∈ {Confirmed, Confirmed on site} → evidence_refs NOT EMPTY C-5, VR-33
K5 received_at ≤ logged_at VR-05, D-25
K6 CaseLink: from ≠ to; both cases same customer; at most one Duplicate of per case VR-10, D-14
K7 CaseEvent is insert-only (no update/delete) Audit; reliable metrics
K8 Case type ≠ Service request → final_severity NOT NULL after triage; billing → final_severity ≠ Hygiene-Critical D-17, F-12
K9 Status enquiries never create Case rows; they create followup_received events on the parent D-10
K10 No Awaiting Confirmation while a task with mandatory = true is Open F-3

5. Event types (CaseEvent.event_type)

case_logged, site_flagged_unverified, classified, reclassified, linked, severity_set, severity_overridden, expedited, customer_update_sent (payload: includes_case_ref), followup_received, handoff_initiated, handoff_accepted, handoff_returned, task_created, task_done, status_changed, hold_started, hold_ended, escalated (payload: trigger, decision), resolution_recorded, confirmation_requested, confirmed, rejected, no_response_closed, closed, reopened, unauthorised_attempt.

07_phase7/analytics_spec.md

Phase 7 — Analytics Specification

All metrics are proposed. PadCare has no structured complaint data today (brief, C-6), so there is no baseline. Targets should be set after 2–3 months of module data.

1. Common definitions (apply to every metric)

Term Definition
Complaint Case with type ∈ {Operational complaint, Billing complaint}. Service requests and account-level concerns are reported separately; status enquiries are not cases (they are follow-ups)
Valid case closure_reason ∉ {Cancelled – Duplicate, Cancelled – Invalid}
Period attribution Volume metrics by received_at; resolution and closure metrics by closed_at; reopen by the closure cohort
Business time Per SlaPolicy, net of hold_started → hold_ended intervals
City The site's city; account-level concerns use the customer's primary_city, or "Multi-city"
Reporting statistic Median and P90 for durations (not the mean: a few long cases skew it)

2. Metrics

# Metric Definition (numerator / denominator) Cut by Question it answers Challenge
M1 Case volume Count of valid cases received in the period Type, sub-category, city, customer, site, channel, severity How much and where? C-6
M2 Category share by city Complaints of a sub-category in a city / all complaints in that city (same period) City × sub-category "Are 40% of complaints missed services in one city?" (brief's example) C-6
M3 Repeat (recurrence) rate Complaints with recurrence_count ≥ 1 at logging (≥ 1 prior same site + sub-category within 90 days) / all complaints received City, customer, site, sub-category Are we fixing causes or symptoms? C-2
M4 First response time received_at → first customer_update_sent with includes_case_ref = true Severity, channel, CS owner How fast do customers hear from us? (R3) C-7
M5 Registration delay received_at → logged_at; plus the share of cases flagged Not logged at receipt Channel, logger role Are issues still getting lost or logged late? C-1
M6 Time to resolution received_at → first resolution_recorded, net of hold Type × severity, city, owner team How fast do we fix? (X1–X4) C-5
M7 SLA compliance Per target Rx/Xx/Vx: cases meeting it / cases where it applied (valid cases only) Target, type, severity, city, owner team Which stage is the bottleneck? C-4, C-7
M8 Time in Assigned and handoff return rate Sum of handoff_initiated → accepted/returned per case; returns / handoffs Receiving team Where do handoffs stall? C-4
M9 Ageing by owner Open cases by current resolution owner (or team) in age buckets (0–1, 2–3, 4–7, > 7 business days) since received_at, plus open tasks by task owner Owner, team, city Who is holding what, for how long? C-4
M10 Customer-confirmed closure rate Closed with reason Confirmed / Confirmed on site ÷ all valid closed cases Type, city, CS owner Is "closed" really closed? C-5
M11 No-response closure rate Closed – No Response / valid closed Type, city How often do we close without confirmation? C-5
M12 Reopen rate Cases closed in period P that were reopened within 14 days / valid cases closed in P (report P only once 14 days have passed) Type, sub-category, resolution team Fix quality C-5
M13 Rejection rate Cases with rejection_count ≥ 1 / cases reaching Awaiting Confirmation Type, resolution team First-time fix C-5
M14 Chase rate Open or closed cases with ≥ 1 followup_received / valid cases; and follow-ups per case CS owner, type Are customers still having to ask? C-7
M15 Silence breaches Cases with ≥ 1 R6 breach / open cases in period CS owner Are we updating proactively? C-7
M16 Escalation rate Cases with ≥ 1 escalated / valid cases; by trigger Trigger, team, city Where do rules have to force action? C-4
M17 Severity override rate Cases where final ≠ system severity / triaged cases; by direction (up / down) and by reporter role CS user, reporter role Is "loudest wins" creeping back? Overrides that cluster on leadership reporters are the signal C-8
M18 Expedite usage Count of expedites by user and customer User, customer Same as M17 C-8
M19 Reclassification rate Cases with ≥ 1 reclassified / triaged cases From → to type Are the classification rules clear? C-3

3. Worked example — the brief's "40% missed services in one city" question

-- M2: share of each complaint sub-category within each city, last quarter
SELECT s.city,
       c.sub_category,
       COUNT(*) AS complaints,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY s.city), 1) AS pct_of_city
FROM case_register c
JOIN site s ON s.site_id = c.site_id
WHERE c.case_type IN ('Operational complaint', 'Billing complaint')
  AND c.received_at >= DATE '2025-07-01' AND c.received_at < DATE '2025-10-01'
  AND COALESCE(c.closure_reason, '') NOT LIKE 'Cancelled%'
GROUP BY s.city, c.sub_category
ORDER BY s.city, pct_of_city DESC;

Answerable only because city (from site), case_type and sub_category are structured and status enquiries are not counted as complaints (D-10).

4. Data quality risks to these metrics

Risk Effect Control
Wrong sub-category M2/M3 distort Short lists; M19 monitored; quarterly review of "Other"
Backdated received_at M4/M5/M6 look worse or better received_at edits are logged; > 30 days needs a reason (VR-06)
Wrong site / unverified sites M3 misses recurrences VR-02/03; unverified site resolved at Triage
No-response closures M10 looks better than reality Reported separately (M11)
Low logging adoption All volumes understated M5 Not logged at receipt share; channel mix trend

5. Views (only after the data above exists)

View Audience Contents
My queue CS, Finance, SE, Ops City Manager Open cases and tasks by computed priority; SLA timers; silence timers
City operations Ops City Manager M1–M3 for the city; M9 ageing; recurrence hotspots (site × sub-category)
Monthly review CS/Ops leadership, KAMs M2, M3, M7, M10, M12, M14, M17; per-account view for KAMs (supports S-05 meetings)

2. Issues found and fixed

ID Where Inconsistency Why it mattered Fix
AU-01 Flow overview, walkthroughs, Challenges Map, traceability The F-3 "linked tasks" insert renumbered §3.3 → 3.4, but the overview and the walkthroughs still cited "3.3 Accept or return" A reviewer following step references in Task 2 would land on the wrong section Overview lists 3.1–3.4; walkthrough acceptance steps cite 3.2; the map cites 3.1–3.4
AU-02 Status table, E-8, E-10, analytics, data model Four vocabularies for closure reasons ("Logged in error" as a reason vs a sub-reason; "No response to information request" vs "No Response") Metrics M10/M11 and the "valid case" filter would be computed differently by different people One canonical list: Confirmed · Confirmed on site · Plan Agreed · No Response · Cancelled – Duplicate · Cancelled – Invalid (+ sub-reason). Displayed as Closed – <reason>
AU-03 Flow §2.5 The "3+ sites" and recurrence escalators applied to all types, so S-05 (multi-site quality trend, no hygiene exposure) would become Hygiene-Critical Same class of error as F-12: severity stops meaning "hygiene exposure" Escalators apply to operational complaints only; billing escalates (F-12); account-level concerns use their own rule (highest open-case severity, else Service-Impacting)
AU-04 Flow §2.4, VR-12, M3, walkthrough A "Recurrence" meant both the link (from the 2nd case) and the escalation flag (from the 3rd); M3 counted ≥ 1 prior while VR-12 fired at ≥ 2 An interviewer asking "what is your repeat rate?" would get two answers Repeat = 2nd case onwards (link + count; M3). Recurrence flag = 3rd case onwards (escalator + root cause)
